sentences.zh: 馬懷素，潤州丹徒人也。

translations.literal: Ma HuaiSu—Ma HuaiSu was a native of Dantu in Run Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: Ma Huai Su was a native of Dantu in Run Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 寓居江都，少師事李善。

translations.literal: He resided in Jiangdu and in his youth took Li Shan as his teacher.
translations.idiomatic: He lived in Jiangdu and in his youth studied under Li Shan.

sentences.zh: 家貧無燈燭，晝采薪蘇，夜燃讀書，遂博覽經史，善屬文。

translations.literal: His family was poor and had no lamps or candles; by day he gathered firewood and kindling, by night he burned them to read, and thus came to read broadly in the classics and histories and was skilled at literary composition.
translations.idiomatic: His family was too poor to afford lamps or candles; by day he gathered firewood and brush, and by night he burned them to read by their light. In this way he came to be widely versed in the classics and histories and skilled at writing.

sentences.zh: 舉進士，又應制舉，登文學優贍科，拜郿尉，四遷左臺監察御史。

translations.literal: He passed the jinshi examination, also responded to the imperial examination, attained the Literary Excellence and Abundant Talent category, was appointed Mei district magistrate, and was transferred four times to Left Censorate investigating censor.
translations.idiomatic: He passed the jinshi examination and also took the special imperial literary examination, placing in the Literary Excellence and Abundant Talent category. He was appointed magistrate of Mei district and was promoted four times to investigating censor of the Left Censorate.

sentences.zh: 長安中，御史大夫魏元忠為張易之所構，配徙嶺表，太子仆崔貞慎、東宮率獨孤祎之餞於郊外。

translations.literal: During the Chang'an period, Censor-in-Chief Wei Yuanzhong was framed by Zhang Yizhi and was banished to the Lingnan region; Grand Master of the Household for the Heir Apparent Cui Zhenshen and Eastern Palace Commandant Dugu Yizhi saw him off in the suburbs.
translations.idiomatic: During the Chang'an era, Censor-in-Chief Wei Yuanzhong was framed by Zhang Yizhi and banished to the far south. Grand Master of the Household for the Heir Apparent Cui Zhenshen and Eastern Palace Commandant Dugu Yizhi gave him a farewell feast outside the city.

sentences.zh: 易之怒，使人誣告貞慎等與元忠同謀，則天令懷素按鞫，遣中使促迫，諷令構成其事，懷素執正不受命。

translations.literal: Yizhi was enraged and had men falsely accuse Zhenshen and the others of plotting with Yuanzhong; Empress Wu ordered HuaiSu to investigate and interrogate, sent palace envoys to press him, and hinted that he should fabricate the case, but HuaiSu held to what was right and would not accept the command.
translations.idiomatic: Yizhi was furious and had men accuse Zhenshen and the others of conspiring with Yuanzhong. Empress Wu ordered Huai Su to investigate the case and sent palace envoys to hurry him along, hinting that he should frame them. Huai Su stood firm and refused to comply.

sentences.zh: 則天怒，召懷素親加詰問，懷素奏曰：「元忠犯罪配流，貞慎等以親故相送，誠為可責，若以為謀反，臣豈誣罔神明？

translations.literal: Empress Wu was angry and summoned HuaiSu to question him in person. HuaiSu memorialized, saying: "Yuanzhong committed a crime and was banished; Zhenshen and the others saw him off because of personal ties—this is indeed blameworthy, but if it is taken as rebellion, how could your servant deceive the divine and bright?
translations.idiomatic: The empress was angry and summoned Huai Su to question him personally. Huai Su replied, "Yuanzhong had committed a crime and was sent into exile; Zhenshen and the others saw him off out of personal regard. That is indeed culpable, but if this is called treason, how could I deceive Heaven itself?

sentences.zh: 昔彭越以反伏誅，欒布奏事於其屍下，漢朝不坐，況元忠罪非彭越，陛下豈加追送之罪。

translations.literal: Formerly Peng Yue was executed for rebellion, yet Luan Bu presented a memorial before his corpse, and the Han court did not punish him—how much less is Yuanzhong's crime that of Peng Yue? How could Your Majesty add guilt for seeing him off?
translations.idiomatic: In former times Peng Yue was executed for treason, yet Luan Bu presented a memorial before his corpse, and the Han court did not punish him. Yuanzhong's offense is nothing like Peng Yue's. Surely Your Majesty would not punish those who merely saw him off.

sentences.zh: 陛下當生殺之柄，欲加之罪，取決聖衷可矣。

translations.literal: Your Majesty holds the power of life and death; if you wish to add guilt, let it be decided by the imperial heart alone.
translations.idiomatic: Your Majesty holds the power of life and death. If you wish to punish them, that is for your sacred judgment alone.

sentences.zh: 若付臣推鞫，臣敢不守陛下之法？」

translations.literal: If you entrust the case to your servant to investigate and interrogate, how would your servant dare not uphold Your Majesty's laws?"
translations.idiomatic: But if you entrust the investigation to me, how could I dare not uphold your laws?"

sentences.zh: 則天意解，貞慎等由是獲免。

translations.literal: The empress's mind was eased, and Zhenshen and the others were thereby spared.
translations.idiomatic: The empress's anger subsided, and Zhenshen and the others were spared.

sentences.zh: 時夏官侍郎李迥秀恃張易之之勢，受納貨賄，懷素奏劾之，迥秀遂罷知政事。

translations.literal: At that time Summer Office Vice Minister Li Huixiu relied on Zhang Yizhi's power and accepted bribes; HuaiSu memorialized to impeach him, and Huixiu was then removed from handling state affairs.
translations.idiomatic: At that time Vice Minister of the Summer Office Li Huixiu, relying on Zhang Yizhi's influence, accepted bribes. Huai Su impeached him, and Huixiu was removed from office.

sentences.zh: 懷素累轉禮部員外郎，與源乾曜、盧懷慎、李傑等充十道黜陟使。

translations.literal: HuaiSu was repeatedly transferred to Rituals Department vice director and, with Yuan Ganyao, Lu Huaishen, Li Jie, and others, served as commissioners for promotion and demotion in the ten circuits.
translations.idiomatic: Huai Su rose through several posts to vice director of the Ministry of Rites and, together with Yuan Ganyao, Lu Huaishen, Li Jie, and others, served as commissioners for promotion and demotion in the ten circuits.

sentences.zh: 懷素處事平恕，當時稱之。

translations.literal: HuaiSu handled affairs with fairness and forbearance, and he was praised at the time.
translations.idiomatic: Huai Su handled affairs with fairness and forbearance, and was widely praised.

sentences.zh: 使還，遷考功員外郎。

translations.literal: When the mission returned, he was transferred to vice director of the Bureau of Evaluations.
translations.idiomatic: When the commission returned, he was promoted to vice director of the Bureau of Evaluations.

sentences.zh: 時貴戚縱恣，請托公行，懷素無所阿順，典舉平允，擢拜中書舍人。

translations.literal: At that time the noble kin were unrestrained and patronage was openly practiced; HuaiSu did not curry favor with anyone, conducted examinations fairly, and was promoted to Secretariat drafter.
translations.idiomatic: At that time the imperial kin were unrestrained and patronage was openly traded. Huai Su would not curry favor with anyone, conducted the examinations fairly, and was promoted to Secretariat drafter.

sentences.zh: 開元初，為戶部侍郎，加銀青光祿大夫，累封常山縣公，三遷秘書監，兼昭文館學士。

translations.literal: At the beginning of the Kaiyuan era he became vice minister of the Ministry of Revenue, was given the silver-blue glory grand master title, was repeatedly enfeoffed as Duke of Changshan county, was transferred three times to director of the Secretariat, and concurrently served as academician of the Zhaowen Hall.
translations.idiomatic: Early in the Kaiyuan era he became vice minister of revenue, was granted the silver-blue glory grand master title, was enfeoffed as Duke of Changshan county, was promoted three times to director of the Secretariat, and concurrently served as an academician of the Zhaowen Hall.

sentences.zh: 懷素雖居吏職，而篤學，手不釋卷，謙恭謹慎，深為玄宗所禮，令與左散騎常侍褚無量同為侍讀。

translations.literal: Although HuaiSu held an administrative post, he was devoted to learning and never put down his books; he was humble, respectful, and cautious, and was deeply honored by Emperor Xuanzong, who ordered him to serve jointly with Left Regular Attendant Chu Wuliang as imperial reader.
translations.idiomatic: Though he held an administrative post, Huai Su was devoted to learning and never put down his books. Humble and careful, he was deeply honored by Emperor Xuanzong, who appointed him and Left Regular Attendant Chu Wuliang as joint imperial readers.

sentences.zh: 每次閣門，則令乘肩輿以進。

translations.literal: Each time he passed the palace gate, he was ordered to enter in a shoulder-borne sedan chair.
translations.idiomatic: Each time he came to the palace gate, he was allowed to enter in a sedan chair borne on men's shoulders.

sentences.zh: 上居別館，以路遠，則命宮中乘馬，或親自送迎，以申師資之禮。

translations.literal: When the emperor resided at a separate lodge and the road was long, he ordered that HuaiSu ride a horse within the palace, or would personally see him off and welcome him back, thereby displaying the rites due a teacher.
translations.idiomatic: When the emperor was staying at a separate lodge and the distance was great, he had Huai Su ride within the palace grounds, or would personally escort him there and back, thereby honoring him as his teacher.

sentences.zh: 是時秘書省典籍散落，條疏無敘，懷素上疏曰：「南齊已前墳籍，舊編王儉《七志》。

translations.literal: At that time the books in the Secretariat were scattered and their entries lacked order. HuaiSu submitted a memorial, saying: "For tomes before the Southern Qi, the old compilation was Wang Jian's Seven Records.
translations.idiomatic: At that time the books in the Secretariat were scattered and their catalogues were in disorder. Huai Su submitted a memorial saying, "For works before the Southern Qi, the old catalogue was Wang Jian's Seven Records.

sentences.zh: 已後著述，其數盈多，《隋志》所書，亦未詳悉。

translations.literal: Writings after that are exceedingly numerous, and even what the Sui Bibliography records is not complete in detail.
translations.idiomatic: Writings since then are exceedingly numerous, and even the Sui Bibliography does not record them fully.

sentences.zh: 或古書近出，前誌闕而未編；

translations.literal: Some ancient books have only recently appeared, and earlier catalogues omitted them and did not register them;
translations.idiomatic: Some ancient books have only recently come to light, and earlier catalogues left them unrecorded;

sentences.zh: 或近人相傳，浮詞鄙而猶記。

translations.literal: some works handed down among recent men are frivolous in wording and base, yet are still recorded.
translations.idiomatic: some works handed down among recent authors are frivolous and vulgar, yet are still listed.

sentences.zh: 若無編錄，難辯淄、澠。

translations.literal: Without compilation and registration, it is hard to distinguish the Zi from the Sheng.
translations.idiomatic: Without a proper catalogue, it is hard to tell the turbid from the clear.

sentences.zh: 望括檢近書篇目，並前誌所遺者，續王儉《七志》，藏之秘府。」

translations.literal: I hope that recent books' titles may be gathered and checked, together with those omitted by earlier catalogues, to continue Wang Jian's Seven Records and store them in the secret repository."
translations.idiomatic: I ask that the titles of recent books be gathered and checked, together with those omitted by earlier catalogues, to continue Wang Jian's Seven Records and store the result in the imperial library."

sentences.zh: 上於是召學涉之士國子博士尹知章等，分部撰錄，並刊正經史，粗創首尾。

translations.literal: The emperor thereupon summoned learned men such as National University erudite Yin Zhizhang, assigned them by section to compile and record, and also to collate and correct the classics and histories, roughly establishing a beginning and end.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor then summoned learned scholars including National University erudite Yin Zhizhang, assigned them by section to compile and catalogue the collection, and also to collate the classics and histories, thus establishing the project in outline.

sentences.zh: 會懷素病卒，年六十，上特為之舉哀，廢朝一日，贈潤州刺史，謚曰文。

translations.literal: It happened that HuaiSu died of illness at age sixty; the emperor specially mourned him, suspended court for one day, posthumously appointed him governor of Run Prefecture, and gave him the posthumous title Wen.
translations.idiomatic: Huai Su then died of illness at the age of sixty. The emperor mourned him in person, suspended court for a day, posthumously appointed him governor of Run Prefecture, and gave him the posthumous title Wen.

sentences.zh: 褚無量，字弘度，杭州鹽官人也。

translations.literal: Chu Wuliang—Chu Wuliang, style Hongdu, was a native of Yanguan in Hang Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: Chu Wuliang, styled Hongdu, was a native of Yanguan in Hang Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 幼孤貧，勵誌好學。

translations.literal: In youth he was orphaned and poor, but he strengthened his will and loved learning.
translations.idiomatic: Orphaned and poor in his youth, he nevertheless resolved to study diligently.

sentences.zh: 家近臨平湖，時湖中有龍鬥，傾裏闬就觀之，無量時年十二，讀書晏然不動。

translations.literal: His home was near Linping Lake; at one time dragons fought in the lake, and the whole neighborhood rushed out to watch, but Wuliang, then twelve years old, read his book calmly without moving.
translations.idiomatic: His home lay near Linping Lake. Once when dragons were said to be fighting in the lake, the whole neighborhood rushed out to watch, but Wuliang, then twelve, sat reading calmly and did not stir.

sentences.zh: 及長，尤精《三禮》及《史記》，舉明經，累除國子博士。

translations.literal: When he grew up he was especially expert in the Three Rites and the Records of the Grand Historian; he passed the mingjing examination and was repeatedly appointed National University erudite.
translations.idiomatic: When he grew up he became especially expert in the Three Rites and the Records of the Grand Historian. He passed the mingjing examination and was repeatedly appointed erudite of the National University.

sentences.zh: 景龍三年，遷國子司業，兼修文館學士。

translations.literal: In the third year of Jinglong he was transferred to National University vice director and concurrently served as academician of the Xiūwen Hall.
translations.idiomatic: In the third year of the Jinglong era he was promoted to vice director of the National University and concurrently served as an academician of the Xiūwen Hall.

sentences.zh: 是歲，中宗將親祀南郊，詔禮官學士修定儀註。

translations.literal: That year Emperor Zhongzong was to perform the southern suburban sacrifice in person and ordered ritual officials and academicians to revise and fix the ceremonial regulations.
translations.idiomatic: That year Emperor Zhongzong was to perform the southern suburban sacrifice in person and ordered ritual officials and scholars to revise the ceremonial regulations.

sentences.zh: 國子祭酒祝欽明、司業郭山惲皆希旨，請以皇后為亞獻，無量獨與太常博士唐紹、蔣欽緒固爭，以為不可。

translations.literal: National University chancellor Zhu Qinming and vice director Guo Shanyun both sought to please and requested that the empress serve as secondary offerer; Wuliang alone, with Court of Imperial Sacrifices erudite Tang Shao and Jiang Qinxu, firmly argued against it, holding that it could not be done.
translations.idiomatic: National University chancellor Zhu Qinming and vice director Guo Shanyun both sought to please the throne and proposed that the empress serve as secondary offerer. Wuliang alone, with Court of Imperial Sacrifices erudites Tang Shao and Jiang Qinxu, argued firmly that this was impermissible.

sentences.zh: 無量建議曰：夫郊祀者，明王之盛事，國家之大禮。

translations.literal: Wuliang submitted a memorial, saying: "Suburban sacrifice is the great undertaking of an enlightened king and the great ritual of the state."
translations.idiomatic: Wuliang submitted a memorial, saying: "Suburban sacrifice is the great undertaking of an enlightened king and the great ritual of the state."

sentences.zh: 行其禮者，不可以臆斷，不可以情求，皆上順天心，下符人事，欽若稽古，率由舊章，然後可以交神明，可以膺福祐。

translations.literal: Those who perform this ritual must not decide by guesswork or seek it through private feeling; all must accord above with the mind of Heaven and below with human affairs, reverently examine antiquity, and follow established statutes—only then can they join with the spirits and receive blessings and protection.
translations.idiomatic: Those who perform this ritual must not decide by guesswork or seek it through private inclination. All must accord above with the mind of Heaven and below with human affairs, reverently examine antiquity, and follow established statutes—only then can they commune with the spirits and receive blessings.

sentences.zh: 然禮文雖眾，莫如《周禮》。

translations.literal: Though ritual texts are many, none surpass the Rites of Zhou.
translations.idiomatic: Though ritual texts are many, none surpass the Rites of Zhou.

sentences.zh: 《周禮》者，周公致太平之書，先聖極由衷之典，法天地而行教化，辯方位而敘人倫。

translations.literal: The Rites of Zhou is the book by which the Duke of Zhou brought the realm to peace—the utmost canon of heartfelt sincerity handed down by the former sages; it takes Heaven and Earth as its model to carry out moral transformation and distinguishes directions and places to set forth human relations.
translations.idiomatic: The Rites of Zhou is the book by which the Duke of Zhou brought the realm to peace—the utmost canon of heartfelt sincerity handed down by the former sages. It takes Heaven and Earth as its model to carry out moral transformation and distinguishes directions and places to set forth human relations.

sentences.zh: 其義可以幽贊神明，其文可以經緯邦國，備物致用，其可忽乎！

translations.literal: Its meaning can secretly assist the spirits; its text can weave together the state—preparing things for their use: how can it be neglected!
translations.idiomatic: Its meaning can secretly assist the spirits; its text can weave together the state. In preparing things for their use, how can it be neglected!

sentences.zh: 至如冬至圓丘，祭中最大，皇后內主，禮位甚尊。

translations.literal: As for the round mound at the winter solstice, among sacrifices it is the greatest; the empress rules within and her ritual rank is very exalted.
translations.idiomatic: As for the round mound at the winter solstice, among sacrifices it is the greatest. The empress rules within, and her ritual rank is very exalted.

sentences.zh: 若合郊天助祭，則當具著禮典。

translations.literal: If she were to join in assisting at the suburban sacrifice to Heaven, this ought to be fully set forth in the ritual canon.
translations.idiomatic: If she were to join in assisting at the suburban sacrifice to Heaven, this ought to be fully set forth in the ritual canon.

sentences.zh: 今遍檢《周官》，無此儀制。

translations.literal: Now, searching through the Offices of Zhou, there is no such ceremony.
translations.idiomatic: Now, searching through the Offices of Zhou, there is no such ceremony.

sentences.zh: 蓋由祭天南郊，不以地配，唯將始祖為主，不以祖妣配天，故唯皇帝親行其禮，皇后不合預也。

translations.literal: This is because when sacrificing to Heaven at the southern suburb, Earth is not taken as consort; only the founding ancestor is taken as chief recipient, and the founding ancestress is not paired with Heaven—therefore only the emperor personally performs the ritual, and the empress should not take part.
translations.idiomatic: This is because when sacrificing to Heaven at the southern suburb, Earth is not taken as consort. Only the founding ancestor is taken as chief recipient, and the founding ancestress is not paired with Heaven. Therefore only the emperor personally performs the ritual, and the empress should not take part.

sentences.zh: 謹按《大宗伯》職云：「若王不祭祀，則攝位。」

translations.literal: Respectfully examining the duties of the Grand Minister of Sacrifices, it says: "If the king does not perform the sacrifice, then one acts in his place."
translations.idiomatic: Respectfully examining the duties of the Grand Minister of Sacrifices, it says: "If the king does not perform the sacrifice, then one acts in his place."

sentences.zh: 《註》云：「王有故，代行其祭事。」

translations.literal: The commentary says: "If the king has reason for absence, another performs the sacrifice in his stead."
translations.idiomatic: The commentary says: "If the king has reason for absence, another performs the sacrifice in his stead."

sentences.zh: 下文云：「凡大祭祀，王後不與，則攝而薦豆籩，徹。」

translations.literal: The text below says: "In all great sacrifices, if the queen consort does not participate, then one acts in her place to present the beans and baskets and remove them."
translations.idiomatic: The text below says: "In all great sacrifices, if the queen consort does not participate, then one acts in her place to present the beans and baskets and remove them."

sentences.zh: 若皇后合助祭，承此下文，即當云「若不祭祀，則攝而薦豆籩。」

translations.literal: If the empress were to join in assisting at the sacrifice, following this text below, it ought to say: "If she does not perform the sacrifice, then one acts in her place to present the beans and baskets."
translations.idiomatic: If the empress were to join in assisting at the sacrifice, following this text below, it ought to say: "If she does not perform the sacrifice, then one acts in her place to present the beans and baskets."

sentences.zh: 今於文上更起凡，則是別生餘事。

translations.literal: Now, if a new general heading were raised above the text, that would be to introduce a separate matter.
translations.idiomatic: Now, if a new general heading were raised above the text, that would be to introduce a separate matter.

sentences.zh: 夫事與上異，則別起凡。

translations.literal: When a matter differs from what precedes, a separate general heading is raised.
translations.idiomatic: When a matter differs from what precedes, a separate general heading is raised.

sentences.zh: 凡者，生上起下之名，不專系於本職。

translations.literal: "General heading" (fan) is a name for what generates what precedes and raises what follows; it is not exclusively tied to one's proper office.
translations.idiomatic: "General heading" (fan) is a name for what generates what precedes and raises what follows; it is not exclusively tied to one's proper office.

sentences.zh: 《周禮》一部之內，此例極多，備在文中，不可具錄。

translations.literal: Within the whole Rites of Zhou this pattern is extremely numerous; all are in the text and cannot all be recorded.
translations.idiomatic: Within the whole Rites of Zhou this pattern is extremely numerous. All are in the text and cannot all be recorded.

sentences.zh: 又王後助祭，親薦豆籩而不徹。

translations.literal: Moreover, when the queen consort assists at sacrifice, she personally presents the beans and baskets but does not remove them.
translations.idiomatic: Moreover, when the queen consort assists at sacrifice, she personally presents the beans and baskets but does not remove them.

sentences.zh: 案《九嬪》職云：「凡祭，贊後薦，徹豆籩。」

translations.literal: Examining the duties of the Nine Consorts, it says: "In all sacrifices, assist the queen consort in presenting and remove the beans and baskets."
translations.idiomatic: Examining the duties of the Nine Consorts, it says: "In all sacrifices, assist the queen consort in presenting and remove the beans and baskets."

sentences.zh: 《註》云：「後進之而不徹。」

translations.literal: The commentary says: "The queen consort advances them but does not remove them."
translations.idiomatic: The commentary says: "The queen consort advances them but does not remove them."

sentences.zh: 則知中徹者，為宗伯生文。

translations.literal: Thus we know that the removal in the middle of the text is wording generated by the Minister of Sacrifices.
translations.idiomatic: Thus we know that the removal in the middle of the text is wording generated by the Minister of Sacrifices.

sentences.zh: 若宗伯攝祭，則宗伯親徹，不別使人。

translations.literal: If the Minister of Sacrifices acts in the king's place at the sacrifice, then the Minister personally removes the offerings and does not send another person.
translations.idiomatic: If the Minister of Sacrifices acts in the king's place at the sacrifice, then the Minister personally removes the offerings and does not send another person.

sentences.zh: 又案「外宗掌宗廟之祀，王後不與，則贊宗伯」。

translations.literal: Again examining: "The outer clan manages sacrifices at the ancestral temple; if the queen consort does not participate, then assist the Minister of Sacrifices."
translations.idiomatic: Again examining: "The outer clan manages sacrifices at the ancestral temple; if the queen consort does not participate, then assist the Minister of Sacrifices."

sentences.zh: 此之一文，與上相證。

translations.literal: This passage and the above mutually confirm each other.
translations.idiomatic: This passage and the above mutually confirm each other.

sentences.zh: 何以明之？

translations.literal: How is this made clear?
translations.idiomatic: How is this made clear?

sentences.zh: 案外宗唯掌宗廟祭祀，不掌郊天，足明此文是宗廟祭也。

translations.literal: Examining further: the outer clan manages only ancestral-temple sacrifices, not suburban sacrifice to Heaven—sufficient to show this text concerns ancestral-temple sacrifice.
translations.idiomatic: Examining further: the outer clan manages only ancestral-temple sacrifices, not suburban sacrifice to Heaven—sufficient to show this text concerns ancestral-temple sacrifice.

sentences.zh: 案王後行事，總在《內宰》職中。

translations.literal: Examining the actions of the queen consort, they are all summarized in the duties of the Palace Steward.
translations.idiomatic: Examining the actions of the queen consort, they are all summarized in the duties of the Palace Steward.

sentences.zh: 檢其職文，唯云：「大祭祀，後稞獻則贊，瑤爵亦如之。」

translations.literal: Checking the text of those duties, it only says: "In great sacrifices, when the queen consort performs the unhusked-grain offering, assist her; the jade goblet is the same."
translations.idiomatic: Checking the text of those duties, it only says: "In great sacrifices, when the queen consort performs the unhusked-grain offering, assist her; the jade goblet is the same."

sentences.zh: 《鄭註》云：「謂祭宗廟也。」

translations.literal: Zheng Xuan's commentary says: "This refers to sacrificing at the ancestral temple."
translations.idiomatic: Zheng Xuan's commentary says: "This refers to sacrificing at the ancestral temple."

sentences.zh: 《註》所以知者，以文雲「稞獻」，祭天無稞，以此得知。

translations.literal: The reason the commentary knows this is that the text says "unhusked-grain offering," and there is no unhusked grain in sacrifice to Heaven—by this it is known.
translations.idiomatic: The reason the commentary knows this is that the text says "unhusked-grain offering," and there is no unhusked grain in sacrifice to Heaven—by this it is known.

sentences.zh: 又祭天之器，則用陶匏，亦無瑤爵，《註》以此得知是宗廟也。

translations.literal: Moreover, vessels for sacrifice to Heaven use pottery and gourds; there are also no jade goblets—the commentary knows by this that it is the ancestral temple.
translations.idiomatic: Moreover, vessels for sacrifice to Heaven use pottery and gourds. There are also no jade goblets—the commentary knows by this that it is the ancestral temple.

sentences.zh: 又內司服掌王後六服，無祭天之服；

translations.literal: Moreover, the Palace Wardrobe Mistress manages the queen consort's six garments, and there are no garments for sacrificing to Heaven;
translations.idiomatic: Moreover, the Palace Wardrobe Mistress manages the queen consort's six garments, and there are no garments for sacrificing to Heaven;

sentences.zh: 而巾車職掌王後之五輅，亦無後祭天之輅；

translations.literal: and the Chariot Master manages the queen consort's five carriages, and there is also no carriage for the queen consort's sacrifice to Heaven;
translations.idiomatic: and the Chariot Master manages the queen consort's five carriages, and there is also no carriage for the queen consort's sacrifice to Heaven;

sentences.zh: 祭天七獻，無後亞獻。

translations.literal: in sacrifice to Heaven there are seven offerings, and no secondary offering by the queen consort.
translations.idiomatic: in sacrifice to Heaven there are seven offerings, and no secondary offering by the queen consort.

sentences.zh: 以此諸文參之，故知後不合助祭天也。

translations.literal: Comparing these various texts, we know the queen consort should not join in assisting at sacrifice to Heaven.
translations.idiomatic: Comparing these various texts, we know the queen consort should not join in assisting at sacrifice to Heaven.

sentences.zh: 唯《漢書》《郊祀志》則有天地合祭，皇后預享之事，此則西漢末代，強臣擅朝，悖亂彜倫，黷神諂祭，不經之典，事涉誣神。

translations.literal: Only in the "Treatise on Suburban Sacrifices" in the Book of Han are there matters of combined sacrifice to Heaven and Earth and the empress sharing in the offering—this belongs to the last age of Western Han, when powerful ministers monopolized the court, violated normative relations, dishonored the spirits with fawning sacrifice, an uncanonical rite involving deceit of the spirits.
translations.idiomatic: Only in the "Treatise on Suburban Sacrifices" in the Book of Han are there matters of combined sacrifice to Heaven and Earth and the empress sharing in the offering. This belongs to the last age of Western Han, when powerful ministers monopolized the court, violated normative relations, dishonored the spirits with fawning sacrifice—an uncanonical rite involving deceit of the spirits.

sentences.zh: 故《易傳》曰：「誣神者，殃及三代。」

translations.literal: Therefore the Commentary on the Changes says: "Those who deceive the spirits bring calamity upon three generations."
translations.idiomatic: Therefore the Commentary on the Changes says: "Those who deceive the spirits bring calamity upon three generations."

sentences.zh: 《太誓》曰：「正稽古立功立事，可以永年，承天之大律。」

translations.literal: The Great Declaration says: "Correctly examining antiquity, establishing merit and undertaking affairs, one can enjoy long years and inherit Heaven's great ordinance."
translations.idiomatic: The Great Declaration says: "Correctly examining antiquity, establishing merit and undertaking affairs, one can enjoy long years and inherit Heaven's great ordinance."

sentences.zh: 斯史策之良誡，豈可不知。

translations.literal: These are excellent admonitions in the historical records—how can one not know them?
translations.idiomatic: These are excellent admonitions in the historical records—how can one not know them?

sentences.zh: 今南郊禮儀，事不稽古，忝守經術，不敢默然。

translations.literal: Now the southern-suburb ritual does not examine antiquity; holding to the classics despite my unworthiness, I dare not remain silent.
translations.idiomatic: Now the southern-suburb ritual does not examine antiquity. Holding to the classics despite my unworthiness, I dare not remain silent.

sentences.zh: 請旁詢碩儒，俯摭舊典，采曲臺之故事，行圓丘之正儀，使聖朝葉昭曠之塗，天下知文物之盛，豈不幸甚。

translations.literal: I request that learned scholars be consulted on all sides, old canons be gathered, precedents from the Terrace of Song be adopted, and the correct ceremony of the round mound be performed, so that the sage dynasty may tread the broad bright path and all under Heaven may know the splendor of culture—would this not be a great fortune?
translations.idiomatic: I request that learned scholars be consulted on all sides, old canons be gathered, precedents from the Terrace of Song be adopted, and the correct ceremony of the round mound be performed, so that the sage dynasty may tread the broad bright path and all under Heaven may know the splendor of culture—would this not be a great fortune?

sentences.zh: 時左僕射韋巨源等阿旨，葉同欽明之議，竟不從無量所奏。

translations.literal: At that time Left Vice Director Wei Juyuan and others curried favor; they followed Qinming's proposal and in the end did not adopt what Wuliang had memorialized.
translations.idiomatic: At that time Left Vice Director Wei Juyuan and others curried favor with the court and sided with Qinming's proposal, and in the end Wuliang's memorial was not accepted.

sentences.zh: 尋以母老請停官歸侍。

translations.literal: Soon afterward, because his mother was old, he requested to leave office and return home to attend her.
translations.idiomatic: Soon afterward, because his mother was elderly, he asked to leave office and return home to care for her.

sentences.zh: 景雲初，玄宗在春宮，召拜國子司業，兼皇太子侍讀，嘗撰《翼善記》以進之，皇太子降書嘉勞，賫絹四十匹。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Jingyun, when Xuanzong was in the Eastern Palace, he was summoned and appointed National University vice director and concurrently imperial reader to the crown prince; he once compiled Record of Assisting in Goodness and presented it, and the crown prince issued a letter of praise and reward, bestowing forty bolts of silk.
translations.idiomatic: Early in the Jingyun era, when Xuanzong was crown prince, Wuliang was summoned as vice director of the National University and concurrently as the crown prince's reader. He once compiled the Record of Assisting in Goodness and presented it to the prince, who replied with a letter of praise and rewarded him with forty bolts of silk.

sentences.zh: 太極元年，皇太子國學親釋奠，令無量講《老經》、《禮記》，各隨端立義，博而且辯，觀者嘆服焉。

translations.literal: In the first year of Taiji the crown prince personally performed the libation sacrifice at the National University and ordered Wuliang to lecture on the Laozi and the Book of Rites; in each section he set forth the meaning as the text required, broadly and yet with eloquence, and the observers sighed in admiration.
translations.idiomatic: In the first year of the Taiji era the crown prince personally performed the libation sacrifice at the National University and had Wuliang lecture on the Laozi and the Book of Rites. In each section he developed the meaning as the text required, with breadth and eloquence, and the audience marveled.

sentences.zh: 既畢，進授銀青光祿大夫，兼賜以章服，並彩絹百段。

translations.literal: When it was finished, he was advanced and given the silver-blue glory grand master title, together with bestowal of official robes and insignia, and also one hundred sections of colored silk.
translations.idiomatic: When the lectures were finished, he was promoted to silver-blue glory grand master and was also granted official robes and insignia, together with one hundred bolts of colored silk.

sentences.zh: 玄宗即位，遷郯王傅，兼國子祭酒。

translations.literal: When Xuanzong took the throne, he was transferred to tutor of the Prince of Tan and concurrently appointed National University chancellor.
translations.idiomatic: When Xuanzong ascended the throne, Wuliang was appointed tutor to the Prince of Tan and concurrently chancellor of the National University.

sentences.zh: 尋以師傅恩遷左散騎常侍，仍兼國子祭酒，封舒國公，實封二百戶。

translations.literal: Soon afterward, because of his favor as tutor, he was transferred to Left Regular Attendant, still concurrently National University chancellor, enfeoffed as Duke of Shu state, with a substantive fief of two hundred households.
translations.idiomatic: Soon afterward, in recognition of his service as tutor, he was promoted to Left Regular Attendant while retaining the chancellorship of the National University, enfeoffed as Duke of Shu, with a substantive fief of two hundred households.

sentences.zh: 未幾，丁憂解職，廬於墓側。

translations.literal: Before long he entered mourning for a parent, left office, and built a mourning hut beside the tomb.
translations.idiomatic: Before long he entered mourning, resigned his post, and built a hut beside his parent's tomb.

sentences.zh: 其所植松柏，時有鹿犯之，無量泣而言曰：「山中眾草不少，何忍犯吾先塋樹哉！」

translations.literal: The pines and cypresses he had planted were at times damaged by deer. Wuliang wept and said: "There is no lack of grass in the mountains—how can you bear to harm the trees at my forebears' grave!"
translations.idiomatic: The pines and cypresses he had planted were sometimes damaged by deer. Wuliang wept and said, "There is no lack of grass in the mountains—how can you bear to harm the trees at my ancestors' grave?"

sentences.zh: 因通夕守護。

translations.literal: He therefore kept watch through the night.
translations.idiomatic: He then kept watch through the night.

sentences.zh: 俄有群鹿馴狎，不復侵害，無量因此終身不食鹿肉。

translations.literal: Before long a herd of deer became tame and no longer caused harm; because of this Wuliang for the rest of his life did not eat deer meat.
translations.idiomatic: Before long a herd of deer became tame and did no further harm, and from that time Wuliang never ate deer meat for the rest of his life.

sentences.zh: 服闋，召拜左散騎常侍，復為侍讀。

translations.literal: When mourning ended he was summoned and appointed Left Regular Attendant and again made imperial reader.
translations.idiomatic: When his mourning ended he was summoned back as Left Regular Attendant and again appointed imperial reader.

sentences.zh: 以其年老，每隨仗出入，特許緩行，又為造腰輿，令內給使輿於內殿。

translations.literal: Because he was old, whenever he followed the imperial guard in and out he was specially permitted to walk slowly; a waist sedan was also made for him, and inner attendants were ordered to carry him in the inner halls.
translations.idiomatic: Because of his age, whenever he attended court he was specially permitted to walk slowly. A waist sedan was made for him, and palace attendants were ordered to carry him within the inner halls.

sentences.zh: 無量頻上書陳時政得失，多見納用。

translations.literal: Wuliang frequently submitted memorials setting forth the gains and losses of current policy, and many of them were adopted.
translations.idiomatic: Wuliang frequently submitted memorials on the strengths and failings of current policy, and many of his recommendations were adopted.

sentences.zh: 又嘗手敕褒美，賜物二百段。

translations.literal: He was also once praised in an imperial autograph edict and given two hundred sections of goods.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor also once praised him in a personal edict and rewarded him with two hundred bolts of goods.

sentences.zh: 無量以內庫舊書，自高宗代即藏在宮中，漸致遺逸，奏請繕寫刊校，以弘經籍之道。

translations.literal: Wuliang noted that old books in the inner storehouse, kept in the palace since Emperor Gaozong's time, had gradually been lost, and memorialized requesting copying, collation, and correction in order to expand the way of the classics and records.
translations.idiomatic: Wuliang observed that old books in the inner storehouse, kept in the palace since the time of Emperor Gaozong, had gradually been lost. He memorialized requesting that they be copied and collated in order to advance the cause of the classics.

sentences.zh: 玄宗令於東都乾元殿前施架排次，大加搜寫，廣采天下異本。

translations.literal: Emperor Xuanzong ordered that at the eastern capital, before the Qianyuan Hall, shelves be set up and books arranged in order; a great effort was made to search for and copy texts, and unusual editions from throughout the realm were widely gathered.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Xuanzong ordered shelves set up before the Qianyuan Hall in the eastern capital, books arranged in order, and a major effort made to search out and copy texts, widely gathering unusual editions from across the realm.

sentences.zh: 數年間，四部充備，仍引公卿已下入殿前，令縱觀焉。

translations.literal: Within several years the four sections were fully stocked, and the emperor also led the ministers and others down before the hall and had them view the collection freely.
translations.idiomatic: Within a few years the four bibliographic sections were fully stocked, and the emperor led ministers and officials down before the hall to view the collection freely.

sentences.zh: 開元六年駕還，又敕無量於麗正殿以續前功。

translations.literal: In the sixth year of Kaiyuan, when the imperial carriage returned, he again ordered Wuliang at the Lizheng Hall to continue the earlier work.
translations.idiomatic: In the sixth year of Kaiyuan, when the emperor returned to the capital, he again ordered Wuliang to continue the project at the Lizheng Hall.

sentences.zh: 皇太子及郯王嗣直等五人，年近十歲，尚未就學，無量繕寫《論語》、《孝經》各五本以獻。

translations.literal: The crown prince and the Prince of Tan, Sizhi, and four others were nearly ten years old and had not yet begun formal study; Wuliang copied five each of the Analects and the Classic of Filial Piety and presented them.
translations.idiomatic: The crown prince, the Prince of Tan Sizhi, and four others were nearly ten and had not yet begun formal study. Wuliang copied five each of the Analects and the Classic of Filial Piety and presented them.

sentences.zh: 上覽之曰：「吾知無量意無量。」

translations.literal: The emperor, on reading them, said: "I know Wuliang's meaning is boundless."
translations.idiomatic: The emperor, on reading them, said, "I know what Wuliang means—and his meaning is boundless."

sentences.zh: 遽令選經明篤行之士國子博士郤恆通郭謙光、左拾遺潘元祚等，為太子及郯王已下侍讀。

translations.literal: He immediately ordered that men learned in the classics and of steadfast conduct be selected—National University erudites Xi Hengtong and Guo Qianguang, Left Reminder Pan Yuanzuo, and others—to serve as readers to the crown prince and the princes below the Prince of Tan.
translations.idiomatic: He immediately ordered scholars learned in the classics and of steadfast conduct to be selected—National University erudites Xi Hengtong and Guo Qianguang, Left Reminder Pan Yuanzuo, and others—to serve as readers to the crown prince and the younger princes.

sentences.zh: 七年，詔太子就國子監行齒胄之禮，無量登座說經，百僚集觀，禮畢，賞賜甚厚。

translations.literal: In the seventh year an edict ordered the crown prince to go to the National University to perform the cap-and-armor ceremony; Wuliang ascended the seat and lectured on the classics, the hundred officials gathered to watch, and when the rite was finished the rewards were very generous.
translations.idiomatic: In the seventh year the crown prince was ordered to the National University to perform the cap-and-armor ceremony. Wuliang ascended the lectern to expound the classics while the officials gathered to watch. When the ceremony was finished, the rewards were very generous.

sentences.zh: 明年，無量病卒，年七十五。

translations.literal: The next year Wuliang died of illness at age seventy-five.
translations.idiomatic: The following year Wuliang died of illness at the age of seventy-five.

sentences.zh: 臨終遺言以麗正寫書未畢為恨。

translations.literal: On his deathbed his final words were that he regretted that the copying of books at Lizheng was not yet finished.
translations.idiomatic: On his deathbed his last words were that he regretted the copying of books at Lizheng was not yet finished.

sentences.zh: 上為舉哀，廢朝兩日，贈禮部尚書，謚曰文。

translations.literal: The emperor mourned him, suspended court for two days, posthumously appointed him minister of rites, and gave him the posthumous title Wen.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor mourned him, suspended court for two days, posthumously appointed him minister of rites, and gave him the posthumous title Wen.

sentences.zh: 初，無量與馬懷素俱為侍讀，顧待甚厚；

translations.literal: Earlier, when Wuliang and Ma HuaiSu had both served as imperial readers, they were favored and treated very generously;
translations.idiomatic: Earlier, when Wuliang and Ma Huai Su had both served as imperial readers, they had been favored and treated with great generosity;

sentences.zh: 及無量等卒後，秘書少監康子原、國子博士侯行果等又入侍講，雖屢加賞賜，而禮遇不逮褚焉。

translations.literal: after Wuliang and the others died, Secretariat vice director Kang Ziyuan, National University erudite Hou Xingguo, and others again entered to lecture, and although rewards were repeatedly increased, the courtesy shown did not reach that given to Chu.
translations.idiomatic: after Wuliang and the others died, Secretariat vice director Kang Ziyuan, National University erudite Hou Xingguo, and others again served as lecturers. Although they were repeatedly rewarded, the courtesy shown them did not equal what had been accorded Chu.

sentences.zh: 劉子玄，本名知幾，楚州刺史胤之族孫也。

translations.literal: Liu Zixuan—Liu Zixuan, original name Zhiji, was a clansman of Chu Prefecture governor Yinzhi.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Zixuan, whose original name was Zhiji, was a clansman of Chu Prefecture governor Liu Yinzhi.

sentences.zh: 少與兄知柔俱以詞學知名，弱冠舉進士，授獲嘉主簿。

translations.literal: In youth he and his elder brother Zhirou were both famed for literary learning; at the capping age he passed the jinshi examination and was appointed Huojia chief clerk.
translations.idiomatic: In his youth he and his elder brother Zhirou were both famed for literary learning. At twenty he passed the jinshi examination and was appointed chief clerk of Huojia.

sentences.zh: 證聖年，有制文武九品已上各言時政得失，知幾上表陳四事，詞甚切直。

translations.literal: In the Zhengsheng year an edict ordered civil and military officials of the ninth rank and above each to speak on the gains and losses of current policy; Zhiji submitted a memorial setting forth four matters, his wording very blunt and direct.
translations.idiomatic: In the Zhengsheng year an edict required civil and military officials of the ninth rank and above to comment on current policy. Zhiji submitted a memorial on four matters in very blunt and direct language.

sentences.zh: 是時官爵僭濫而法網嚴密，士類競為趨進而多陷刑戮，知幾乃著《思慎賦》以刺時，且以見意。

translations.literal: At that time offices and titles were excessively bestowed while the legal net was strict; gentlemen strove to advance and many fell into punishment and execution. Zhiji therefore composed Reflections on Caution to satirize the age and also to express his intent.
translations.idiomatic: At that time offices and titles were lavished without restraint while the law was harsh; scholars scrambled for advancement and many fell victim to punishment. Zhiji therefore wrote Reflections on Caution to satirize the age and make his views known.

sentences.zh: 鳳閣侍郎蘇味道、李嶠見而嘆曰：「陸機《豪士》所不及也。」

translations.literal: Phoenix Pavilion Vice Minister Su Weidao and Li Jiao, on reading it, sighed and said: "Even Lu Ji's Bold Heroes does not reach this."
translations.idiomatic: Phoenix Pavilion Vice Ministers Su Weidao and Li Jiao, on reading it, exclaimed, "Even Lu Ji's Bold Heroes does not equal this."

sentences.zh: 知幾長安中累遷左史，兼修國史。

translations.literal: During Chang'an, Zhiji was repeatedly transferred to Left Historian and concurrently compiled the national history.
translations.idiomatic: During the Chang'an era Zhiji was repeatedly promoted to Left Historian and concurrently compiled the national history.

sentences.zh: 擢拜鳳閣舍人，修史如故。

translations.literal: He was promoted and appointed Phoenix Pavilion drafter, compiling history as before.
translations.idiomatic: He was promoted to Phoenix Pavilion drafter and continued compiling history as before.

sentences.zh: 景龍初，再轉太子中允，依舊修國史。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Jinglong he was again transferred to crown prince palace aide and still compiled the national history as before.
translations.idiomatic: Early in the Jinglong era he was again transferred to crown prince palace aide and continued compiling the national history.

sentences.zh: 時侍中韋巨源紀處訥、中書令楊再思、兵部尚書宗楚客、中書侍郎蕭至忠並監修國史，知幾以監修者多，甚為國史之弊。

translations.literal: At that time Palace Attendant Wei Juyuan, Ji Chune, Chief Minister Yang Zaisi, Minister of War Zong Chuke, and Secretariat Vice Minister Xiao Zhizhong all supervised compilation of the national history; Zhiji regarded the great number of supervisors as a serious defect in the national history.
translations.idiomatic: At that time Palace Attendant Wei Juyuan, Ji Chune, Chief Minister Yang Zaisi, Minister of War Zong Chuke, and Secretariat Vice Minister Xiao Zhizhong all supervised compilation of the national history. Zhiji regarded the great number of supervisors as a serious flaw in the work.

sentences.zh: 蕭至忠又嘗責知幾著述無課，知幾於是求罷史任，奏記於至忠曰：

translations.literal: Xiao Zhizhong also once reproached Zhiji for composing without measurable progress; Zhiji thereupon sought to resign his historiographical post and submitted a note to Zhizhong, saying:
translations.idiomatic: Xiao Zhizhong also once reproached Zhiji for producing little despite his post. Zhiji thereupon sought to resign his historiographical duties and submitted a note to Zhizhong, saying:

sentences.zh: 僕自策名士伍，待罪朝列，三為史臣，再入東觀，竟不能勒成國典，貽彼後來者，何哉？

translations.literal: Your servant, since entering the ranks of eminent scholars and awaiting punishment in the court ranks, has three times been a historiographer and twice entered the Eastern Pavilion, yet in the end could not complete the national canon—what shall be left to those who come after?
translations.idiomatic: I have been among the eminent scholars and have served in the court ranks, three times a historiographer and twice in the Eastern Pavilion, yet in the end I could not complete the national chronicle. What shall I leave to those who come after?

sentences.zh: 靜言思之，其不可者五也。

translations.literal: Reflecting quietly on this, there are five reasons why it cannot be done.
translations.idiomatic: On quiet reflection, there are five reasons why it cannot be done.

sentences.zh: 何者？

translations.literal: What are they?
translations.idiomatic: What are they?

sentences.zh: 古之國史，皆出自一家，如魯、漢之丘明、子長，晉、齊之董狐、南史，鹹能立言不朽，藏諸名山，未聞藉以眾功，方雲絕筆。

translations.literal: Ancient national histories all came from a single hand, as Qiuming and Zichang of Lu and Han, or Dong Hu and the Southern Historian of Jin and Qi—all could establish words that do not perish and store them in famous mountains; one has not heard that by relying on the merit of the multitude one could then say the brush was laid down.
translations.idiomatic: The national histories of antiquity all came from a single author, such as Qiuming and Sima Qian of Lu and Han, or Dong Hu and the Southern Historian of Jin and Qi. All were able to compose words that endure and store them in the storied mountains. One never hears that a history was finished only by pooling many men's work.

sentences.zh: 唯後漢東觀，大集群儒，而著述無主，條章靡立。

translations.literal: Only the Eastern Pavilion of Later Han gathered many Confucians together, yet composition had no master and regulations were not established.
translations.idiomatic: Only at the Eastern Pavilion of Later Han were many scholars gathered together, yet there was no chief author and no established regulations.

sentences.zh: 由是伯度譏其不實，公理以為可焚，張、蔡二子紀之於當代，傅、范兩家嗤之於後葉。

translations.literal: Because of this, Bodu mocked its lack of truth, Gongli held that it should be burned, the two masters Zhang and Cai recorded this in their own time, and the two families Fu and Fan sneered at it in later generations.
translations.idiomatic: Because of this, Bodu mocked its lack of truth, Gongli thought it ought to be burned, Zhang and Cai recorded the fact in their own day, and the families of Fu and Fan sneered at it in later ages.

sentences.zh: 今史司取士，有倍東京，人自以為荀、袁，家自稱為政、駿。

translations.literal: Today the historiographical office selects scholars at more than double the number of the Eastern Capital; each man thinks himself a Xun or Yuan, each household calls itself Zheng or Jun.
translations.idiomatic: Today the historiographical office recruits scholars at more than twice the number used at the Eastern Capital. Each man fancies himself a Xun or a Yuan, each household styles itself Zheng or Jun.

sentences.zh: 每欲記一事，載一言，皆閣筆相視，含毫不斷。

translations.literal: Whenever they wish to record one event or set down one sentence, all lay down the brush and look at one another, holding the tip in the mouth without deciding.
translations.idiomatic: Whenever they wish to record an event or set down a sentence, they all lay down their brushes and look at one another, nib in mouth, unable to decide.

sentences.zh: 故首白可期，而汗青無日。

translations.literal: Thus gray hair may be expected, yet the day of the green bamboo slips never comes.
translations.idiomatic: Thus one may expect to grow old, yet the day when the chronicle is written in green never comes.

sentences.zh: 其不可一也。

translations.literal: This is the first reason why it cannot be done.
translations.idiomatic: This is the first reason why it cannot be done.

sentences.zh: 前漢郡國計書，先上太史，副上丞相；

translations.literal: In Former Han, the commandery and kingdom accounts were first submitted to the Grand Historian and a copy submitted to the chancellor;
translations.idiomatic: In Former Han, the commandery and kingdom statistical reports were first submitted to the Grand Historian and a copy to the chancellor;

sentences.zh: 後漢公卿所撰，始集公府，乃上蘭臺。

translations.literal: in Later Han what the ministers composed was first gathered in the public offices and only then sent up to the Orchid Terrace.
translations.idiomatic: in Later Han what the ministers composed was first gathered in the public offices and only then sent up to the Orchid Terrace.

sentences.zh: 由是史官所修，載事為博。

translations.literal: Because of this, what the historiographers compiled recorded events very broadly.
translations.idiomatic: Because of this, what the historiographers compiled was very full in its coverage of events.

sentences.zh: 原自近古，此道不行，史臣編錄，唯自詢采。

translations.literal: Tracing back from recent antiquity, this practice is not followed; historiographers compile and record only by inquiring and gathering on their own.
translations.idiomatic: Tracing back from recent antiquity, this practice has lapsed; historiographers compile records only by making inquiries on their own.

sentences.zh: 而左右二史，闕註起居；

translations.literal: Yet the Left and Right Historians lack notes on daily conduct;
translations.idiomatic: Yet the Left and Right Historians keep no notes on daily conduct;

sentences.zh: 衣冠百家，罕通行狀。

translations.literal: among the hundred families of officials and gentry, biographical summaries are rarely circulated.
translations.idiomatic: among the families of officials and gentry, biographical summaries are rarely circulated.

sentences.zh: 求風俗於州郡，視聽不該；

translations.literal: When seeking customs in the prefectures and commanderies, what is seen and heard does not cover the whole;
translations.idiomatic: When seeking local customs in the prefectures and commanderies, what one sees and hears does not cover the whole;

sentences.zh: 討沿革於臺閣，簿籍難見。

translations.literal: when investigating continuities and changes in the ministries, registers and documents are hard to see.
translations.idiomatic: when investigating institutional continuities in the ministries, registers and documents are hard to obtain.

sentences.zh: 雖使尼父再出，猶且成其管窺，況限以中才，安能遂其博物。

translations.literal: Even if the Master were to appear again, he would still achieve only a bamboo-tube view; how much less, constrained by middling talent, could one accomplish comprehensive learning?
translations.idiomatic: Even if Confucius were to appear again, he could achieve only a narrow view through a bamboo tube. How much less, constrained by middling talent, could one achieve comprehensive learning?

sentences.zh: 其不可二也。

translations.literal: This is the second reason why it cannot be done.
translations.idiomatic: This is the second reason why it cannot be done.

sentences.zh: 昔董狐之書法也，以示於朝；

translations.literal: Formerly when Dong Hu recorded the execution of the law, he displayed it in court;
translations.idiomatic: Formerly, when Dong Hu recorded the execution of the law, he displayed it in court;

sentences.zh: 南史之書弒也，執簡以往。

translations.literal: when the Southern Historian recorded regicide, he carried the bamboo slip and went forward.
translations.idiomatic: when the Southern Historian recorded regicide, he carried his bamboo slip and went forward.

sentences.zh: 而近代史局，皆通籍禁門，幽居九重，欲人不見。

translations.literal: But in recent times the historiographical bureau, all having registry access to the forbidden gates, dwell secluded within the ninefold palace, wishing that no one see them.
translations.idiomatic: But in recent times the historiographical bureau, all having access to the forbidden gates, dwell secluded within the inner palace, wishing that no one see them.

sentences.zh: 尋其義者，由杜彼顏面，防諸請謁故也。

translations.literal: Seeking the meaning of this, it is because they shut off others' faces and guard against various requests and visits.
translations.idiomatic: The reason, on reflection, is to shut others out and guard against requests and visits.

sentences.zh: 然今館中作者，多士如林，皆願長喙，無聞舌。

translations.literal: Yet today's authors in the bureau are scholars numerous as a forest; all wish to lengthen their beaks, and none are heard to stick out their tongues.
translations.idiomatic: Yet today's authors in the bureau are as numerous as trees in a forest; all wish to speak at length, and none are heard to speak frankly.

sentences.zh: 倘有五始初成，一字加貶，言未絕口而朝野具知，筆未棲毫而搢紳鹹誦。

translations.literal: If the Five Beginnings were just completed and one character of censure added, before the words left the mouth court and commoners alike would know, and before the brush rested on the ink the gentry would all recite it.
translations.idiomatic: If the Five Beginnings were just completed and a single word of censure added, before the words left one's mouth court and commoners alike would know, and before the brush touched the page the gentry would all be reciting it.

sentences.zh: 夫孫盛實錄，取嫉權門；

translations.literal: Sun Sheng's True Record incurred the jealousy of powerful houses;
translations.idiomatic: Sun Sheng's True Record incurred the jealousy of powerful families;

sentences.zh: 王韶直書，見讎貴族。

translations.literal: Wang Shao's straightforward writing made him hated by the nobility.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Shao's straightforward writing made him hated by the nobility.

sentences.zh: 人之情也，能無畏乎！

translations.literal: It is human nature—how could one not fear!
translations.idiomatic: Such is human nature—how could one not fear!

sentences.zh: 其不可三也。

translations.literal: This is the third reason why it cannot be done.
translations.idiomatic: This is the third reason why it cannot be done.

sentences.zh: 古者刊定一史，纂成一家，體統各殊，指歸鹹別。

translations.literal: In antiquity, when a history was revised and fixed, it was compiled by a single school; each had its own form and system, and its aims were all distinct.
translations.idiomatic: In antiquity, when a history was revised and fixed, it was compiled by a single author; each had its own form and system, and its aims were all distinct.

sentences.zh: 夫《尚書》之教也，以疏通知遠為主；

translations.literal: The teaching of the Documents takes making the distant known through the near as its main point;
translations.idiomatic: The teaching of the Documents takes making the distant known through the near as its main point;

sentences.zh: 《春秋》之義也，以懲惡勸善為先。

translations.literal: the meaning of the Spring and Autumn takes punishing evil and encouraging good as its first priority.
translations.idiomatic: the meaning of the Spring and Autumn takes punishing evil and encouraging good as its first priority.

sentences.zh: 《史記》則退處士而進奸雄，《漢書》則抑忠臣而飾主闕。

translations.literal: The Records of the Grand Historian demotes recluses and advances villainous heroes; the Book of Han suppresses loyal ministers and glosses over the ruler's faults.
translations.idiomatic: The Records of the Grand Historian demotes recluses and advances villainous heroes; the Book of Han suppresses loyal ministers and glosses over the ruler's faults.

sentences.zh: 斯並曩賢得失之例，良史是非之準，作者言之詳矣。

translations.literal: These are all examples of former worthies' gains and losses, standards of right and wrong for good historians; the authors have spoken of them in detail.
translations.idiomatic: These are all examples of how former worthies succeeded or failed, standards of right and wrong for good historians; the authors have spoken of them in detail.

sentences.zh: 頃史官註記，多取稟監修，楊令公則雲「必須直詞」，宗尚書則雲「宜多隱惡」。

translations.literal: Recently historiographers' annotations mostly take instructions from the supervising compilers; Lord Yang said "straight words are required," while Minister Zong said "evil should mostly be concealed."
translations.idiomatic: Recently historiographers' annotations mostly follow instructions from the supervising compilers; Lord Yang said "straight words are required," while Minister Zong said "evil should mostly be concealed."

sentences.zh: 十羊九牧，其事難行；

translations.literal: Ten sheep and nine herdsmen—the affair is hard to carry out;
translations.idiomatic: Ten sheep and nine herdsmen—the task is hard to carry out;

sentences.zh: 一國三公，適從焉在？

translations.literal: one state with three dukes—where is the one to follow?
translations.idiomatic: one state with three dukes—whom is one to follow?

sentences.zh: 其不可四也。

translations.literal: This is the fourth reason why it cannot be done.
translations.idiomatic: This is the fourth reason why it cannot be done.

sentences.zh: 竊以史置監修，雖無古式，尋其名號，可得而言。

translations.literal: I venture to think that placing supervising compilers over history, though without an ancient model, may be understood by searching out the meaning of the title.
translations.idiomatic: I venture to think that placing supervising compilers over history, though without an ancient model, may be understood by considering the meaning of the title.

sentences.zh: 夫言監者，蓋總領之義耳。

translations.literal: To speak of supervision is roughly the sense of overall command.
translations.idiomatic: To speak of supervision is roughly the sense of overall command.

sentences.zh: 如創紀編年，則年有斷限；

translations.literal: If creating annals by year, then years should have clear limits;
translations.idiomatic: If creating annals by year, then years should have clear limits;

sentences.zh: 草傳敘事，則事有豐約。

translations.literal: if drafting biographies and narrating events, then events should have fullness and brevity.
translations.idiomatic: if drafting biographies and narrating events, then events should have due fullness or brevity.

sentences.zh: 或可略而不略，或應書而不書，此失刊削之例也。

translations.literal: What may be abbreviated may not be abbreviated, or what ought to be recorded may not be recorded—this is a failure of the rules of editing.
translations.idiomatic: What may be abbreviated may not be abbreviated, or what ought to be recorded may not be recorded—this is a failure of editorial discipline.

sentences.zh: 屬詞比事，勞逸宜均；

translations.literal: In arranging words and comparing events, labor and ease should be balanced;
translations.idiomatic: In arranging words and comparing events, labor and ease should be balanced;

sentences.zh: 揮鉛奮墨，勤惰須等。

translations.literal: in wielding the lead and exerting the ink, diligence and idleness must be equal.
translations.idiomatic: in wielding brush and ink, diligence and idleness must be equal.

sentences.zh: 某帙某篇，付之此職；

translations.literal: Such-and-such a fascicle and chapter should be entrusted to this office;
translations.idiomatic: Such-and-such a fascicle and chapter should be entrusted to this office;

sentences.zh: 某紀某傳，歸之此官。

translations.literal: such-and-such an annal or biography should be assigned to this official.
translations.idiomatic: such-and-such an annal or biography should be assigned to this official.

sentences.zh: 此銓配之理也。

translations.literal: This is the principle of weighing and assigning.
translations.idiomatic: This is the principle of weighing and assigning duties.

sentences.zh: 斯並宜明立科條，審定區域，倘人思自勉，則書可立成。

translations.literal: All of these ought to have regulations clearly established and domains carefully fixed; if men think to encourage themselves, then the book can be quickly completed.
translations.idiomatic: All of these ought to have regulations clearly established and domains carefully fixed; if men are moved to exert themselves, then the book can be quickly completed.

sentences.zh: 今監之者既不指授，修之者又無遵奉。

translations.literal: Today the supervisors neither give directions, nor do the compilers have anything to follow.
translations.idiomatic: Today the supervisors give no directions, and the compilers have nothing to follow.

sentences.zh: 用使爭學茍且，務相推避，坐變炎涼，徒延歲月。

translations.literal: This causes men to compete in learning to be slipshod, striving to push tasks onto one another, sitting while hot and cold change, and merely prolonging the months and years.
translations.idiomatic: This causes men to compete in being slipshod, striving to push tasks onto one another, sitting idle while seasons pass, and merely prolonging the months and years.

sentences.zh: 其不可五也。

translations.literal: This is the fifth reason why it cannot be done.
translations.idiomatic: This is the fifth reason why it cannot be done.

sentences.zh: 凡此不可，其流實多，一言以蔽，三隅自反。

translations.literal: Of all these impossibilities the currents are truly many; one word covers them, and from three corners one returns to oneself.
translations.idiomatic: Of all these impossibilities the ramifications are truly many; one word covers them, and from three corners one returns to oneself.

sentences.zh: 而時談物議，焉得笑仆編次無聞者哉！

translations.literal: Yet the talk of the age and the judgment of things—how can they laugh at your servant for compiling without renown!
translations.idiomatic: Yet the talk of the age and public opinion—how can they laugh at me for compiling without renown!

sentences.zh: 比者伏見明公每汲汲於勸誘，勤勤於課績。

translations.literal: Recently I have observed that you, sir, are ever urgently encouraging and diligently pressing for results.
translations.idiomatic: Recently I have observed that you, sir, are ever urgently encouraging and diligently pressing for results.

sentences.zh: 或云墳籍事重，努力用心；

translations.literal: Some say the matter of tomes and records is weighty and one must strive with heart;
translations.idiomatic: Some say the matter of tomes and records is weighty and one must strive with all one's heart;

sentences.zh: 或云歲序已淹，何時輟手？

translations.literal: others say the year has already dragged on—when will you lay down the brush?
translations.idiomatic: others say the year has already dragged on—when will you lay down the brush?

sentences.zh: 竊以綱維不舉，而督課徒勤，雖威以次骨之刑，勖以懸金之賞，終不可得也。

translations.literal: I venture to think that if the framework is not raised and supervision is vainly diligent, even if one threatens with punishment short of bone-breaking and encourages with rewards of hanging gold, in the end it cannot be obtained.
translations.idiomatic: I venture to think that if the framework is not established and supervision is vainly diligent, even if one threatens with the harshest punishments and encourages with the richest rewards, in the end nothing can be achieved.

sentences.zh: 語曰：「陳力就列，不能則止。」

translations.literal: The saying goes: "Display your strength and take your place; if you cannot, then stop."
translations.idiomatic: The saying goes, "Display your strength and take your place; if you cannot, then stop."

sentences.zh: 仆所以比者布懷知己，歷詆群公，屢辭載筆之官，願罷記言之職者，正為此耳。

translations.literal: The reason your servant has recently laid open his thoughts to one who knows him, repeatedly criticized the lords, often declined the office of bearing the brush, and wished to resign the post of recording words is precisely this.
translations.idiomatic: The reason I have recently laid open my thoughts to one who knows me, repeatedly criticized the lords, often declined the office of bearing the brush, and wished to resign the post of recording words is precisely this.

sentences.zh: 當今朝號得人，國稱多士。

translations.literal: The present court is called to have obtained men; the state is said to have many scholars.
translations.idiomatic: The present court is said to have obtained men; the state is said to have many scholars.

sentences.zh: 蓬山之下，良直差肩；

translations.literal: Beneath Mount Peng, the upright stand shoulder to shoulder;
translations.idiomatic: Beneath Mount Peng, the upright stand shoulder to shoulder;

sentences.zh: 蕓閣之中，英奇接武。

translations.literal: Within the Tallow-Tree Pavilion, the extraordinary follow in martial array.
translations.idiomatic: Within the Tallow-Tree Pavilion, the extraordinary follow one after another.

sentences.zh: 仆既功虧刻鵠，筆未獲麟，徒殫太官之膳，虛索長安之米，乞以本職，還其舊居，多謝簡書，請避賢路。

translations.literal: Your servant has already failed in carving the swan, and his brush has not obtained the unicorn; he merely exhausts the Grand Steward's meals and vainly seeks Chang'an's rice. I beg to keep my original post, return to my old position, decline many letters of appointment, and ask to yield the path of worthies.
translations.idiomatic: I have already failed in carving the swan, and my brush has not obtained the unicorn; I merely exhaust the Grand Steward's meals and vainly draw Chang'an's rice. I beg to keep my original post, return to my old position, decline further appointments, and ask to yield the path of worthies.

sentences.zh: 惟明公足下哀而許之。

translations.literal: May you, sir, pity me and grant this.
translations.idiomatic: May you, sir, pity me and grant this.

sentences.zh: 至忠惜其才，不許解史任。

translations.literal: Zhizhong valued his talent and did not permit him to resign his historiographical post.
translations.idiomatic: Zhizhong valued his talent and did not permit him to resign his historiographical post.

sentences.zh: 宗楚客嫉其正直，謂諸史官曰：「此人作書如是，欲置我何地！」

translations.literal: Zong Chuke resented his uprightness and said to the historiographers: "When this man writes books like this, where does he mean to place me!"
translations.idiomatic: Zong Chuke resented his uprightness and said to the historiographers, "When this man writes books like this, where does he mean to place me!"

sentences.zh: 時知幾又著《史通子》二十卷，備論史策之體。

translations.literal: At that time Zhiji also composed Generalities on Historiography in twenty scrolls, fully discussing the forms of historical writing.
translations.idiomatic: At that time Zhiji also composed Generalities on Historiography in twenty scrolls, fully discussing the forms of historical writing.

sentences.zh: 太子右庶子徐堅深重其書，嘗云：「居史職者，宜置此書於座右。」

translations.literal: Crown Prince Right Vice Director Xu Jian deeply valued the book and once said: "Those who hold historiographical office ought to place this book at their seat's right hand."
translations.idiomatic: Crown Prince Right Vice Director Xu Jian deeply valued the book and once said, "Those who hold historiographical office ought to place this book at their right hand."

sentences.zh: 知幾自負史才，常慨時無知己，乃委國史於著作郎吳兢，別撰《劉氏家史》十五卷、《譜考》三卷。

translations.literal: Zhiji prided himself on historiographical talent and often lamented that the age had no one who knew him; he therefore entrusted the national history to composition director Wu Jing and separately compiled the Liu Clan Family History in fifteen scrolls and Genealogical Inquiry in three scrolls.
translations.idiomatic: Zhiji prided himself on historiographical talent and often lamented that the age had no one who understood him. He therefore entrusted the national history to composition director Wu Jing and separately compiled the Liu Clan Family History in fifteen scrolls and Genealogical Inquiry in three scrolls.

sentences.zh: 推漢氏為陸終苗裔，非堯之後。

translations.literal: He traced the Han clan as descendants of Lu Zhong, not descendants of Yao.
translations.idiomatic: He traced the Han clan as descendants of Lu Zhong, not descendants of Yao.

sentences.zh: 彭城叢亭裏諸劉，出自宣帝子楚孝王囂曾孫司徒居巢侯劉愷之後，不承楚元王交。

translations.literal: The various Liu of Congting Lane in Pengcheng came from the line of Emperor Xuan's son, King Xiao of Chu, Biao, the great-grandson's grandson Minister of Works Marquis of Juchao Liu Kai, and did not descend from King Yuan of Chu, Jiao.
translations.idiomatic: The various Liu of Congting Lane in Pengcheng came from the line of Emperor Xuan's son King Xiao of Chu Biao, through his great-great-grandson Minister of Works Marquis of Juchao Liu Kai, and did not descend from King Yuan of Chu Jiao.

sentences.zh: 皆按據明白，正前代所誤，雖為流俗所譏，學者服其該博。

translations.literal: All were based on clear evidence and corrected errors of former ages; although mocked by common opinion, scholars acknowledged his comprehensive learning.
translations.idiomatic: All were based on clear evidence and corrected errors of former ages. Although mocked by common opinion, scholars acknowledged his comprehensive learning.

sentences.zh: 初，知幾每雲若得受封，必以居巢為名，以紹司徒舊邑；

translations.literal: Earlier Zhiji often said that if he received a fief, he would certainly take Juchao as its name, to continue the old domain of the Minister of Works;
translations.idiomatic: Earlier Zhiji often said that if he received a fief, he would certainly take Juchao as its name, to continue the old domain of the Minister of Works;

sentences.zh: 後以修《則天實錄》功，果封居巢縣子。

translations.literal: later, because of his merit in compiling the Veritable Record of Empress Zetian, he was indeed enfeoffed as Viscount of Juchao county.
translations.idiomatic: later, because of his merit in compiling the Veritable Record of Empress Zetian, he was indeed enfeoffed as Viscount of Juchao county.

sentences.zh: 又鄉人以知幾兄弟六人進士及第，文學知名，改其鄉里為高陽鄉居巢里。

translations.literal: Moreover, because the people of his district, seeing that Zhiji and his five brothers all passed the jinshi examination and were famed for literary learning, changed his native district to Gaoyang township, Juchao lane.
translations.idiomatic: Moreover, because the people of his district, seeing that Zhiji and his five brothers all passed the jinshi examination and were famed for literary learning, changed his native district to Gaoyang township, Juchao lane.

sentences.zh: 景雲中，累遷太子左庶子，兼崇文館學士，仍依舊修國史，加銀青光祿大夫。

translations.literal: During Jingyun he was repeatedly transferred to crown prince left vice director, concurrently academician of the Chongwen Hall, still compiling the national history as before, and given the silver-blue glory grand master title.
translations.idiomatic: During the Jingyun era he was repeatedly promoted to crown prince left vice director and concurrently academician of the Chongwen Hall, continuing to compile the national history and granted the silver-blue glory grand master title.

sentences.zh: 時玄宗在東宮，知幾以名音類上名，乃改子玄。

translations.literal: At that time Xuanzong was in the Eastern Palace; because Zhiji's name sounded like the emperor's taboo name, he changed it to Zixuan.
translations.idiomatic: At that time Xuanzong was crown prince. Because Zhiji's name sounded like the emperor's taboo name, he changed it to Zixuan.

sentences.zh: 二年，皇太子將親釋奠於國學，有司草儀註，令從塵皆乘馬著衣冠。

translations.literal: In the second year the crown prince was to perform the libation sacrifice in person at the National University; the relevant offices drafted ceremonial regulations ordering all followers to ride horses and wear caps and robes.
translations.idiomatic: In the second year the crown prince was to perform the libation sacrifice in person at the National University. The relevant offices drafted ceremonial regulations ordering all followers to ride horses and wear caps and robes.

sentences.zh: 子玄進議曰：古者自大夫已上，皆乘車而以馬為騑服。

translations.literal: Zixuan submitted a proposal, saying: "In antiquity, from grand masters upward, all rode in carriages with horses as paired outriders."
translations.idiomatic: Zixuan submitted a proposal, saying: "In antiquity, from grand masters upward, all rode in carriages with horses as paired outriders."

sentences.zh: 魏、晉已降，迄乎隋代，朝士又駕牛車，歷代經史，具有其事，不可一二言也。

translations.literal: From Wei and Jin downward through the Sui, court gentlemen again drove ox-carts; the classics and histories of successive ages fully record this matter—it cannot be told in a word or two.
translations.idiomatic: From Wei and Jin downward through the Sui, court gentlemen again drove ox-carts. The classics and histories of successive ages fully record this matter—it cannot be told in a word or two.

sentences.zh: 至如李廣北征，解鞍憩息；

translations.literal: As when Li Guang on northern campaign ungirded his saddle and rested;
translations.idiomatic: As when Li Guang on northern campaign ungirded his saddle and rested;

sentences.zh: 馬援南伐，據鞍顧盼。

translations.literal: or Ma Yuan on southern campaign sat his saddle and looked about.
translations.idiomatic: or Ma Yuan on southern campaign sat his saddle and looked about.

sentences.zh: 斯則鞍馬之設，行於軍旅；

translations.literal: This shows that saddles and horses were employed in military campaigns;
translations.idiomatic: This shows that saddles and horses were employed in military campaigns;

sentences.zh: 戎服所乘，貴於便習者也。

translations.literal: what military dress rides values convenience and ease.
translations.idiomatic: what military dress rides values convenience and ease.

sentences.zh: 按江左官至尚書郎而輒輕乘馬，則為御史所彈。

translations.literal: According to the Jiang-left period, if one reached the rank of Palace Gentleman of the Masters of Writing and casually rode a horse, he would be impeached by the censor.
translations.idiomatic: According to the Jiang-left period, if one reached the rank of Palace Gentleman of the Masters of Writing and casually rode a horse, he would be impeached by the censor.

sentences.zh: 又顏延之罷官後，好騎馬出入閭裏，當代稱其放誕。

translations.literal: Again, after Yan Yanzhi left office he liked to ride horses in and out of the lanes, and his contemporaries called him unrestrained.
translations.idiomatic: Again, after Yan Yanzhi left office he liked to ride horses in and out of the lanes, and his contemporaries called him unrestrained.

sentences.zh: 此則專車憑軾，可擐朝衣；

translations.literal: Thus riding a dedicated carriage with hands on the crossbar, one could don court robes;
translations.idiomatic: Thus riding a dedicated carriage with hands on the crossbar, one could don court robes;

sentences.zh: 單馬禦鞍，宜從褻服。

translations.literal: riding a single horse with saddle, one ought to wear informal dress.
translations.idiomatic: riding a single horse with saddle, one ought to wear informal dress.

sentences.zh: 求之近古，灼然之明驗也。

translations.literal: Seeking this in recent antiquity, the proof is clear.
translations.idiomatic: Seeking this in recent antiquity, the proof is clear.

sentences.zh: 自皇家撫運，沿革隨時。

translations.literal: Since our dynasty received the Mandate, institutions have changed with the times.
translations.idiomatic: Since our dynasty received the Mandate, institutions have changed with the times.

sentences.zh: 至如陵廟巡謁，王公冊命，則盛服冠履，乘彼輅車。

translations.literal: As for touring and paying respects at imperial tombs and temples or investiture of princes and dukes, then in full dress with cap and shoes, one rides in that imperial carriage.
translations.idiomatic: As for touring and paying respects at imperial tombs and temples or investiture of princes and dukes, then in full dress with cap and shoes, one rides in that imperial carriage.

sentences.zh: 其士庶有衣冠親迎者，亦時以服箱充馭。

translations.literal: When common gentlemen and commoners went to receive a bride in formal dress, they also sometimes used a carriage box as conveyance.
translations.idiomatic: When common gentlemen and commoners went to receive a bride in formal dress, they also sometimes used a carriage box as conveyance.

sentences.zh: 在於他事，無復乘車，貴賤所行，通用鞍馬而已。

translations.literal: For other matters there was no longer riding in carriages; what noble and mean alike used was saddles and horses only.
translations.idiomatic: For other matters there was no longer riding in carriages. What noble and mean alike used was saddles and horses only.

sentences.zh: 臣伏見比者鑾輿出幸，法駕首途，左右侍臣，皆以朝服乘馬。

translations.literal: Your subject respectfully observes that recently when the imperial carriage went forth, at the start of the formal procession the attendant ministers on left and right all rode horses in court dress.
translations.idiomatic: Your subject respectfully observes that recently when the imperial carriage went forth, at the start of the formal procession the attendant ministers on left and right all rode horses in court dress.

sentences.zh: 夫冠履而出，只可配車而行，今乘車既停，而冠履不易，可謂唯知其一而未知其二也。

translations.literal: Cap and shoes going forth can only properly be paired with riding in a carriage; now riding in carriages has ceased but cap and shoes are not changed—this may be called knowing one thing but not knowing the second.
translations.idiomatic: Cap and shoes going forth can only properly be paired with riding in a carriage. Now riding in carriages has ceased but cap and shoes are not changed—this may be called knowing one thing but not knowing the second.

sentences.zh: 何者？

translations.literal: Why?
translations.idiomatic: Why?

sentences.zh: 褒衣博帶，革履高冠，本非馬上所施，自是車中之服。

translations.literal: Flowing robes and broad belts, leather shoes and tall caps were originally not for use on horseback; they are inherently dress for riding in a carriage.
translations.idiomatic: Flowing robes and broad belts, leather shoes and tall caps were originally not for use on horseback; they are inherently dress for riding in a carriage.

sentences.zh: 必也韈而升鐙，跣以乘鞍，非唯不師古道，亦自取驚今俗。
