translations.literal: If one must don stockings to mount the stirrup or go barefoot to ride the saddle, this is not only failing to follow the ancient way but also inviting shock from present custom.
translations.idiomatic: If one must don stockings to mount the stirrup or go barefoot to ride the saddle, this is not only failing to follow the ancient way but also inviting shock from present custom.

sentences.zh: 求諸折中，進退無可。

translations.literal: Seeking the mean, neither advancing nor retreating is possible.
translations.idiomatic: Seeking the mean, neither advancing nor retreating is possible.

sentences.zh: 且長裾廣袖，襜如翼如，鳴珮行組，鏘鏘奕奕，馳驟於風塵之內，出入於旌棨之間，倘馬有驚逸，人從顛墜，遂使屬車之右，遣履不收，清道之傍，絓驂相續，固以受嗤行路，有損威儀。

translations.literal: Moreover, with long skirts and broad sleeves swaying like wings, girdle pendants and sash ornaments clinking brilliantly, galloping within wind and dust, entering and exiting among banners and halberd-standards—if the horse is startled and bolts, men fall headlong, so that to the right of the attendant carriage shoes are left behind unrecovered, and along the cleared road entangled traces of outriders follow one another—this would indeed draw ridicule from passersby and damage imperial dignity.
translations.idiomatic: Moreover, with long skirts and broad sleeves swaying like wings, girdle pendants and sash ornaments clinking brilliantly, galloping within wind and dust, entering and exiting among banners and halberd-standards—if the horse is startled and bolts, men fall headlong. Shoes are left behind unrecovered to the right of the attendant carriage, and along the cleared road entangled traces of outriders follow one another—this would indeed draw ridicule from passersby and damage imperial dignity.

sentences.zh: 今議者皆云秘閣有《梁武帝南郊圖》，多有危冠乘馬者，此則近代故事，不得謂無其文。

translations.literal: Now those debating all say the palace archives have the "Southern Suburb Picture of Emperor Wu of Liang," with many wearing precarious caps while riding horses—this is a story of recent times and cannot be said to lack documentary basis.
translations.idiomatic: Now those debating all say the palace archives have the "Southern Suburb Picture of Emperor Wu of Liang," with many wearing precarious caps while riding horses. This is a story of recent times and cannot be said to lack documentary basis.

sentences.zh: 臣案此圖是後人所為，非當時所撰。

translations.literal: Your subject maintains this picture was made by later people, not composed at the time.
translations.idiomatic: Your subject maintains this picture was made by later people, not composed at the time.

sentences.zh: 且觀代間有古今圖畫者多矣，如張僧繇畫《群公祖二疏》，而兵士有著芒屩者；

translations.literal: Moreover, among paintings old and new from various ages there are many—such as Zhang Sengyou's "Princes and Dukes Seeing Off the Two Shus," in which soldiers wear straw sandals;
translations.idiomatic: Moreover, among paintings old and new from various ages there are many—such as Zhang Sengyou's "Princes and Dukes Seeing Off the Two Shus," in which soldiers wear straw sandals;

sentences.zh: 閻立本畫《明君入匈奴》，而歸人有著帷帽者。

translations.literal: or Yan Liben's "Bright Lady Entering the Xiongnu," in which returning women wear veiled caps.
translations.idiomatic: or Yan Liben's "Bright Lady Entering the Xiongnu," in which returning women wear veiled caps.

sentences.zh: 夫芒屩出於水鄉，非京華所有；

translations.literal: Straw sandals come from water country, not from the capital region;
translations.idiomatic: Straw sandals come from water country, not from the capital region;

sentences.zh: 帷帽創於隋代，非漢官所作。

translations.literal: veiled caps were created in the Sui, not made by Han officials.
translations.idiomatic: veiled caps were created in the Sui, not made by Han officials.

sentences.zh: 議者豈可征此二畫，以為故實者乎？

translations.literal: Can debaters cite these two paintings as historical fact?
translations.idiomatic: Can debaters cite these two paintings as historical fact?

sentences.zh: 由斯而言，則《梁氏南郊之圖》，義同於此。

translations.literal: Speaking from this, the Liang southern-suburb picture is the same in principle.
translations.idiomatic: Speaking from this, the Liang southern-suburb picture is the same in principle.

sentences.zh: 又傅稱因俗，禮貴緣情。

translations.literal: Again, the Commentary says to follow custom; ritual values conforming to feeling.
translations.idiomatic: Again, the Commentary says to follow custom; ritual values conforming to feeling.

sentences.zh: 殷輅周冕，規模不一；

translations.literal: Yin chariots and Zhou caps—forms are not one;
translations.idiomatic: Yin chariots and Zhou caps—forms are not one;

sentences.zh: 秦冠漢佩，用舍無常。

translations.literal: Qin caps and Han sashes—use and discard have no fixed rule.
translations.idiomatic: Qin caps and Han sashes—use and discard have no fixed rule.

sentences.zh: 況我國家道軼百王，功高萬古，事有不便，理資變通，其乘馬衣冠，竊謂宜從省廢。

translations.literal: Moreover our dynasty's Way surpasses the hundred kings, its merit towers over ten thousand ages—when matters are inconvenient, reason calls for flexible change; riding horses in court dress, your subject ventures to say, ought to be simplified and abandoned.
translations.idiomatic: Moreover our dynasty's Way surpasses the hundred kings and its merit towers over ten thousand ages. When matters are inconvenient, reason calls for flexible change. Riding horses in court dress, your subject ventures to say, ought to be simplified and abandoned.

sentences.zh: 臣懷此異議，其來自久，日不暇給，未及搉楊。

translations.literal: Your subject has held this dissenting view for long; days have not afforded leisure, and he has not yet been able to set it forth.
translations.idiomatic: Your subject has held this dissenting view for long. Days have not afforded leisure, and he has not yet been able to set it forth.

sentences.zh: 今屬殿下親從齒胄，將臨國學，凡有衣冠乘馬，皆憚此行，所以輒進狂言，用申鄙見。

translations.literal: Now, as Your Highness personally follows the crown-prince studies and is about to visit the National University, all who would ride horses in court dress fear this journey—therefore your subject rashly advances these words to state his humble view.
translations.idiomatic: Now, as Your Highness personally follows the crown-prince studies and is about to visit the National University, all who would ride horses in court dress fear this journey. Therefore your subject rashly advances these words to state his humble view.

sentences.zh: 皇太子手令付外宣行，仍編入令，以為常式。

translations.literal: The crown prince issued a personal order to have it promulgated outside and also incorporated into regulations as a permanent form.
translations.idiomatic: The crown prince issued a personal order to have it promulgated and also incorporated it into regulations as a permanent form.

sentences.zh: 開元初，遷左散騎常侍，修史如故。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Kaiyuan he was transferred to Left Regular Attendant and compiled history as before.
translations.idiomatic: Early in the Kaiyuan era he was promoted to Left Regular Attendant and continued compiling history as before.

sentences.zh: 九年，長子貺為太樂令，犯事配流。

translations.literal: In the ninth year his eldest son Bian, Director of the Imperial Music Office, committed an offense and was banished.
translations.idiomatic: In the ninth year his eldest son Bian, Director of the Imperial Music Office, committed an offense and was banished.

sentences.zh: 子玄詣執政訴理，上聞而怒之，由是貶授安州都督府別駕。

translations.literal: Zixuan went to the chief ministers to plead his case; when the emperor heard of it he was angry, and because of this Zixuan was demoted and appointed vice prefect of Anzhou area command.
translations.idiomatic: Zixuan went to the chief ministers to plead his case. When the emperor heard of it he was angry, and Zixuan was demoted to vice prefect of Anzhou.

sentences.zh: 子玄掌知國史，首尾二十餘年，多所撰述，甚為當時所稱。

translations.literal: Zixuan was in charge of the national history for more than twenty years from beginning to end, composed many works, and was greatly praised in his time.
translations.idiomatic: Zixuan was in charge of the national history for more than twenty years, composed many works, and was greatly praised in his time.

sentences.zh: 禮部尚書鄭惟忠嘗問子玄曰：「自古已來，文士多而史才少，何也？」

translations.literal: Minister of Rites Zheng Weizhong once asked Zixuan: "From antiquity until now, literary men have been many but historiographical talents few—why?"
translations.idiomatic: Minister of Rites Zheng Weizhong once asked Zixuan, "From antiquity until now, literary men have been many but historiographical talents few. Why is this?"

sentences.zh: 對曰：「史才須有三長，世無其人，故史才少也。

translations.literal: He replied: "Historiographical talent requires three excellences; the age has no such men, and therefore historiographical talent is few.
translations.idiomatic: He replied, "Historiographical talent requires three excellences. The age has no such men, and therefore historiographical talent is few.

sentences.zh: 三長：謂才也，學也，識也。

translations.literal: The three excellences are: talent, learning, and discernment.
translations.idiomatic: The three excellences are talent, learning, and discernment.

sentences.zh: 夫有學而無才，亦猶有良田百頃，黃金滿籝，而使愚者營生，終不能致於貨殖者矣。

translations.literal: To have learning without talent is also like having a hundred qing of good fields and a coffer full of gold, yet making a fool manage livelihood—in the end one cannot achieve wealth.
translations.idiomatic: To have learning without talent is like having a hundred qing of good fields and a coffer full of gold, yet putting a fool in charge of business—in the end one cannot achieve wealth.

sentences.zh: 如有才而無學，亦猶思兼匠石，巧若公輸，而家無楩楠斧斤，終不果成其宮室者矣。

translations.literal: To have talent without learning is also like wishing to combine the skills of Master Stone and be as clever as Gongshu Ban, yet having no home stocked with hardwood, axes, and adzes—in the end one cannot complete a palace.
translations.idiomatic: To have talent without learning is like wishing to combine the skills of Master Stone and be as clever as Gongshu Ban, yet having no hardwood, axes, or adzes at home—in the end one cannot build a palace.

sentences.zh: 猶須好是正直，善惡必書，使驕主賊臣，所以知懼，此則為虎傅翼，善無可知，所向無敵者矣。

translations.literal: One still needs to love what is upright, record good and evil without fail, and make arrogant rulers and treacherous ministers know fear—this is to give wings to a tiger; with goodness that cannot be known, one goes where none can resist.
translations.idiomatic: One still needs to love what is upright and record good and evil without fail, so that arrogant rulers and treacherous ministers know fear. This is to give wings to a tiger; with goodness that cannot be concealed, one goes where none can resist.

sentences.zh: 脫茍非其才，不可叨居史任。

translations.literal: If one lacks such talent, one must not presumptuously occupy a historiographical post.
translations.idiomatic: If one lacks such talent, one must not presumptuously occupy a historiographical post.

sentences.zh: 自夐古已來，能應斯目者，罕見其人。」

translations.literal: From remote antiquity until now, those who could meet this standard have rarely been seen."
translations.idiomatic: From remote antiquity until now, those who could meet this standard have rarely been seen."

sentences.zh: 時人以為知言。

translations.literal: People of the time regarded this as knowing speech.
translations.idiomatic: People of the time regarded this as wise speech.

sentences.zh: 子玄至安州，無幾而卒，年六十一。

translations.literal: Zixuan reached Anzhou and before long died at age sixty-one.
translations.idiomatic: Zixuan reached Anzhou and before long died at the age of sixty-one.

sentences.zh: 自幼及長，述作不倦，朝有論著，必居其職。

translations.literal: From youth to age he composed without weariness; whenever the court had a work to discuss, he was sure to hold the post.
translations.idiomatic: From youth to old age he composed without weariness. Whenever the court had a work to discuss, he was sure to hold the post.

sentences.zh: 預修《三教珠英》、《文館詞林》、《姓族系錄》，論《孝經》非鄭玄註、《老子》河上公註，修《唐書實錄》，皆行於代，有集三十卷。

translations.literal: He took part in compiling Pearl Splendor of the Three Teachings, Forest of Literary Phrases of the Literature Hall, and Genealogical Records of Clans and Surnames; he argued that the Classic of Filial Piety was not annotated by Zheng Xuan and that the Laozi was not annotated by Duke Riverbank; he compiled the Tang Veritable Record—all circulated in his age—and he had a collected works in thirty scrolls.
translations.idiomatic: He took part in compiling Pearl Splendor of the Three Teachings, Forest of Literary Phrases of the Literature Hall, and Genealogical Records of Clans and Surnames; he argued that the Classic of Filial Piety was not annotated by Zheng Xuan and that the Laozi was not annotated by Duke Riverbank; he compiled the Tang Veritable Record—all circulated in his age—and he had collected works in thirty scrolls.

sentences.zh: 後數年，玄宗敕河南府就家寫《史通》以進，讀而善之，追贈汲郡太守；

translations.literal: Several years later Emperor Xuanzong ordered Henan prefecture to copy Generalities on Historiography at his home and present it; on reading it he approved it and posthumously appointed him governor of Ji commandery;
translations.idiomatic: Several years later Emperor Xuanzong ordered Henan prefecture to copy Generalities on Historiography at his home and present it. On reading it he approved it and posthumously appointed him governor of Ji commandery;

sentences.zh: 尋又贈工部尚書，謚曰文。

translations.literal: soon afterward he was also posthumously appointed minister of works and given the posthumous title Wen.
translations.idiomatic: soon afterward he was also posthumously appointed minister of works and given the posthumous title Wen.

sentences.zh: 兄知柔，少以文學政事，歷荊揚曹益宋海唐等州長史刺史、戶部侍郎、國子司業、鴻臚卿、尚書右丞、工部尚書、東都留守。

translations.literal: His elder brother Zhirou, famed from youth for literary learning and administrative affairs, served successively as chief administrator and governor of Jing, Yang, Cao, Yi, Song, Hai, Tang, and other prefectures, vice minister of revenue, National University vice director, director of the Court for Diplomatic Reception, right vice director of the Secretariat, minister of works, and eastern capital regent.
translations.idiomatic: His elder brother Zhirou, famed from youth for literary learning and administrative affairs, served successively as chief administrator and governor of Jing, Yang, Cao, Yi, Song, Hai, Tang, and other prefectures, vice minister of revenue, National University vice director, director of the Court for Diplomatic Reception, right vice director of the Secretariat, minister of works, and eastern capital regent.

sentences.zh: 卒，贈太子少保，謚曰文。

translations.literal: On his death he was posthumously appointed Junior Tutor to the Heir Apparent and given the posthumous title Wen.
translations.idiomatic: On his death he was posthumously appointed Junior Tutor to the Heir Apparent and given the posthumous title Wen.

sentences.zh: 代傳儒學之業，時人以述作名其家。

translations.literal: For generations they transmitted the work of Confucian learning, and people of the time named their household for composition.
translations.idiomatic: For generations they transmitted the work of Confucian learning, and people of the time named their household for literary composition.

sentences.zh: 子玄子貺、餗、匯、秩、迅、迥，皆知名於時。

translations.literal: Zixuan's sons Bian, Su, Hui, Zhi, Xun, and Jiong were all famed in their time.
translations.idiomatic: Zixuan's sons Bian, Su, Hui, Zhi, Xun, and Jiong were all famed in their time.

sentences.zh: 子玄子 貺貺，博通經史，明天文、律歷、音樂、醫算之術，終於起居郎、修國史。

translations.literal: Zixuan's son Bian—Bian was broadly versed in the classics and histories and understood astronomy, calendrics, music, medicine, and calculation; he ended as Attendant of the Bedchamber and compiler of the national history.
translations.idiomatic: Zixuan's son Bian was broadly versed in the classics and histories and understood astronomy, calendrics, music, medicine, and calculation. He ended his career as Attendant of the Bedchamber and compiler of the national history.

sentences.zh: 撰《六經外傳》三十七卷、《續說苑》十卷、《太樂令壁記》三卷、《真人肘後方》三卷、《天宮舊事》一卷。

translations.literal: He composed Supplementary Traditions of the Six Classics in thirty-seven scrolls, Continuation of the Garden of Sayings in ten scrolls, Wall Record of the Director of Imperial Music in three scrolls, Elbow-Back Prescriptions of the Perfected Man in three scrolls, and Old Affairs of the Heavenly Palace in one scroll.
translations.idiomatic: He composed Supplementary Traditions of the Six Classics in thirty-seven scrolls, Continuation of the Garden of Sayings in ten scrolls, Wall Record of the Director of Imperial Music in three scrolls, Elbow-Back Prescriptions of the Perfected Man in three scrolls, and Old Affairs of the Heavenly Palace in one scroll.

sentences.zh: 子玄子 餗餗，右補闕、集賢殿學士、修國史。

translations.literal: Zixuan's son Su—Su was Right Reminder, academician of the Hall of Assembled Worthies, and compiler of the national history.
translations.idiomatic: Zixuan's son Su was Right Reminder, academician of the Hall of Assembled Worthies, and compiler of the national history.

sentences.zh: 著《史例》三卷、《傳記》三卷、《樂府古題解》一卷。

translations.literal: He wrote Precedents in Historiography in three scrolls, Biographies in three scrolls, and Explication of Ancient Titles in the Music Bureau in one scroll.
translations.idiomatic: He wrote Precedents in Historiography in three scrolls, Biographies in three scrolls, and Explication of Ancient Titles in the Music Bureau in one scroll.

sentences.zh: 子玄子 匯匯，給事中、尚書右丞、左散騎常侍、荊南長沙節度，有集三卷。

translations.literal: Zixuan's son Hui—Hui was Attendant Within, right vice director of the Secretariat, Left Regular Attendant, and Jingnan Changsha military commissioner; he had collected works in three scrolls.
translations.idiomatic: Zixuan's son Hui was Attendant Within, right vice director of the Secretariat, Left Regular Attendant, and Jingnan Changsha military commissioner. He had collected works in three scrolls.

sentences.zh: 子玄子 秩秩，給事中、尚書右丞、國子祭酒。

translations.literal: Zixuan's son Zhi—Zhi was Attendant Within, right vice director of the Secretariat, and National University chancellor.
translations.idiomatic: Zixuan's son Zhi was Attendant Within, right vice director of the Secretariat, and National University chancellor.

sentences.zh: 撰《政典》三十五卷、《止戈記》七卷、《至德新議》十二卷、《指要》三卷。

translations.literal: He composed Administrative Canon in thirty-five scrolls, Record of Ceasing Arms in seven scrolls, New Discussions of Supreme Virtue in twelve scrolls, and Essentials in three scrolls.
translations.idiomatic: He composed Administrative Canon in thirty-five scrolls, Record of Ceasing Arms in seven scrolls, New Discussions of Supreme Virtue in twelve scrolls, and Essentials in three scrolls.

sentences.zh: 論喪紀制度加籩豆，許私鑄錢，改制國學，事各在本志。

translations.literal: His discussions of mourning regulations and adding ritual vessels, permitting private coining, and reforming the National University are each treated in the relevant monographs.
translations.idiomatic: His discussions of mourning regulations and adding ritual vessels, permitting private coining, and reforming the National University are each treated in the relevant monographs.

sentences.zh: 子玄子 迅迅，右補闕，撰《六說》五卷。

translations.literal: Zixuan's son Xun—Xun was Right Reminder and composed Six Discourses in five scrolls.
translations.idiomatic: Zixuan's son Xun was Right Reminder and composed Six Discourses in five scrolls.

sentences.zh: 子玄子 迥迥，諫議大夫、給事中，有集五卷。

translations.literal: Zixuan's son Jiong—Jiong was Remonstrance Grand Master and Attendant Within; he had collected works in five scrolls.
translations.idiomatic: Zixuan's son Jiong was Remonstrance Grand Master and Attendant Within. He had collected works in five scrolls.

sentences.zh: 子玄諸孫貺子浹、滋，匯子贊。

translations.literal: Among Zixuan's grandsons were Bian's sons Jia and Zi, and Hui's son Zan.
translations.idiomatic: Among Zixuan's grandsons were Bian's sons Jia and Zi, and Hui's son Zan.

sentences.zh: 滋，貞元中位至宰輔。

translations.literal: Zi, during the Zhenyuan era, rose to the position of chief minister.
translations.idiomatic: Zi rose to the position of chief minister during the Zhenyuan era.

sentences.zh: 贊，觀察使，自有傳。

translations.literal: Zan was a surveillance commissioner and has his own biography.
translations.idiomatic: Zan was a surveillance commissioner and has his own biography.

sentences.zh: 徐堅徐堅，西臺舍人齊聃子也。

translations.literal: Xu Jian—Xu Jian was the son of Western Terrace drafter Qi Dan.
translations.idiomatic: Xu Jian was the son of Western Terrace drafter Qi Dan.

sentences.zh: 少好學，遍覽經史，性寬厚長者。

translations.literal: In youth he loved learning, read broadly in the classics and histories, and by nature was generous and a man of long standing.
translations.idiomatic: In youth he loved learning, read broadly in the classics and histories, and was by nature generous and steady.

sentences.zh: 進士舉，累授太學。

translations.literal: He passed the jinshi examination and was repeatedly appointed to the Grand Academy.
translations.idiomatic: He passed the jinshi examination and was repeatedly appointed to the Grand Academy.

sentences.zh: 聖歷中，車駕在三陽宮，御史大夫楊再思、太子左庶子王方慶為東都留守，引堅為判官，表奏專以委之。

translations.literal: During the Shenglü era, when the imperial carriage was at the Sanyang Palace, Censor-in-Chief Yang Zaisi and crown prince left vice director Wang Fangqing served as eastern capital regents and brought in Jian as case judge, entrusting memorials and reports to him alone.
translations.idiomatic: During the Shenglü era, when the emperor was at the Sanyang Palace, Censor-in-Chief Yang Zaisi and crown prince left vice director Wang Fangqing served as eastern capital regents and brought in Jian as case judge, entrusting memorials and reports to him alone.

sentences.zh: 方慶善《三禮》之學，每有疑滯，常就堅質問，堅必能征舊說，訓釋詳明，方慶深善之。

translations.literal: Fangqing was skilled in the learning of the Three Rites; whenever he had doubts or difficulties he would go to Jian to question him, and Jian was always able to cite old explanations and interpret them in detail and with clarity, which Fangqing deeply approved.
translations.idiomatic: Fangqing was skilled in the learning of the Three Rites. Whenever he had doubts he would go to Jian to question him, and Jian was always able to cite old explanations and interpret them clearly, which Fangqing deeply approved.

sentences.zh: 又賞其文章典實，常稱曰：「掌綸誥之選也。」

translations.literal: He also prized his literary compositions as canonical and solid and often said: "The choice for drafting imperial edicts."
translations.idiomatic: He also prized his literary compositions as canonical and solid and often said, "The choice for drafting imperial edicts."

sentences.zh: 再思亦曰：「此鳳閣舍人樣，如此才識，走避不得。」

translations.literal: Zaisi also said: "This is the model of a Phoenix Pavilion drafter; with such talent and insight, one cannot avoid promoting him."
translations.idiomatic: Zaisi also said, "This is the model of a Phoenix Pavilion drafter. With such talent and insight, one cannot help but promote him."

sentences.zh: 堅又與給事中徐彥伯、定王府倉曹劉知幾、右補闕張說同修《三教珠英》。

translations.literal: Jian also, with Attendant Within Xu Yanbo, Prince of Ding's warehouse clerk Liu Zhiji, and Right Reminder Zhang Yue, jointly compiled Pearl Splendor of the Three Teachings.
translations.idiomatic: Jian also worked with Attendant Within Xu Yanbo, Prince of Ding's warehouse clerk Liu Zhiji, and Right Reminder Zhang Yue to compile Pearl Splendor of the Three Teachings.

sentences.zh: 時麟臺監張昌宗及成均祭酒李嶠總領其事，廣引文詞之士，日夕談論，賦詩聚會，歷年未能下筆。

translations.literal: At that time Unicorn Terrace director Zhang Changzong and National University chancellor Li Jiao oversaw the affair, widely recruiting men of literary phrasing who talked day and night, composed poetry, and gathered for feasts, yet for years could not put brush to paper.
translations.idiomatic: At that time Unicorn Terrace director Zhang Changzong and National University chancellor Li Jiao oversaw the project, widely recruiting literary men who talked day and night, composed poetry, and gathered for feasts, yet for years could not put brush to paper.

sentences.zh: 堅獨與說構意撰錄，以《文思博要》為本，更加《姓氏》、《親族》二部，漸有條匯。

translations.literal: Jian alone, with Yue, conceived the plan and compiled, taking Literary Reflections and Broad Essentials as the foundation and adding two sections, Surnames and Kinship, gradually bringing order.
translations.idiomatic: Jian alone, with Yue, conceived the plan and compiled, taking Literary Reflections and Broad Essentials as the foundation and adding two sections on surnames and kinship, gradually bringing order to the work.

sentences.zh: 諸人依堅等規制，俄而書成，遷司封員外郎。

translations.literal: The others followed the regulations of Jian and the rest, and before long the book was completed; he was transferred to vice director of the Bureau of Enfeoffments.
translations.idiomatic: The others followed Jian's regulations, and before long the book was completed. He was then promoted to vice director of the Bureau of Enfeoffments.

sentences.zh: 則天又令堅刪改《唐史》，會則天遜位而止。

translations.literal: Empress Wu also ordered Jian to revise the Tang History, but when Empress Wu abdicated the work stopped.
translations.idiomatic: Empress Wu also ordered Jian to revise the Tang History, but when she abdicated the work stopped.

sentences.zh: 神龍初，再遷給事中。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Shenlong he was again transferred to Attendant Within.
translations.idiomatic: Early in the Shenlong era he was again promoted to Attendant Within.

sentences.zh: 時雍州人韋月將上書告武三思不臣之跡，反為三思所陷，中宗即令殺之。

translations.literal: At that time Wei Yuejiang of Yong Prefecture submitted a memorial reporting Wu Sansi's traces of disloyalty, but was instead framed by San Si; Emperor Zhongzong immediately ordered him killed.
translations.idiomatic: At that time Wei Yuejiang of Yong Prefecture submitted a memorial reporting Wu Sansi's disloyalty, but was instead framed by San Si. Emperor Zhongzong immediately ordered him executed.

sentences.zh: 時方盛夏，堅上表曰：「月將誣構良善，故違制命，準其情狀，誠合嚴誅。

translations.literal: It was then high summer. Jian submitted a memorial, saying: "Yuejiang falsely framed the good and therefore violated the imperial command; judging by the circumstances, he indeed deserves severe execution.
translations.idiomatic: It was then high summer. Jian submitted a memorial saying, "Yuejiang falsely framed the innocent and therefore violated the imperial command. Judging by the circumstances, he indeed deserves severe punishment.

sentences.zh: 但今硃夏在辰，天道生長，即從明戮，有乖時令。

translations.literal: But now vermilion summer is in its season and the way of Heaven is growth; to carry out open execution immediately goes against the season.
translations.idiomatic: But now it is high summer, when the way of Heaven is growth. To carry out open execution immediately goes against the season.

sentences.zh: 謹按《月令》：『夏行秋令，則丘隰水潦，禾稼不熟。』

translations.literal: I respectfully cite the Monthly Ordinances: "If in summer one executes autumn's commands, then hills and lowlands flood and grain does not ripen."
translations.idiomatic: I respectfully cite the Monthly Ordinances: "If in summer one executes autumn's commands, then hills and lowlands flood and grain does not ripen."

sentences.zh: 陛下誕膺靈命，中興聖圖，將弘義、軒之風，以光史策之美，豈可非時行戮，致傷和氣哉！

translations.literal: Your Majesty was born to receive the numinous mandate and restored the sacred design; you will spread the winds of Yao and Xuan to brighten the beauty of the historical records—how could you carry out executions out of season and harm harmonious qi!
translations.idiomatic: Your Majesty was born to receive the sacred mandate and restored the imperial design. You will spread the winds of Yao and Xuan to brighten the historical records. How could you carry out executions out of season and harm harmonious qi!

sentences.zh: 君舉必書，將何以訓？

translations.literal: The ruler's actions are always recorded—by what will you instruct?
translations.idiomatic: The ruler's actions are always recorded—what lesson will this teach?

sentences.zh: 伏願詳依國典，許至秋分，則知恤刑之規，冠於千載；

translations.literal: I humbly wish that you carefully follow the state canon and permit delay until the autumn equinox; then the regulation of compassionate punishment would crown a thousand years;
translations.idiomatic: I humbly wish that you carefully follow the state canon and permit delay until the autumn equinox. Then the regulation of compassionate punishment would crown a thousand years;

sentences.zh: 哀矜之惠，洽乎四海。」

translations.literal: the grace of pity and compassion would reach the four seas."
translations.idiomatic: the grace of pity and compassion would reach the four seas."

sentences.zh: 中宗納堅所奏，遂令決杖，配流嶺表。

translations.literal: Emperor Zhongzong accepted Jian's memorial and therefore ordered beating with the rod and banishment to the Lingnan region.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Zhongzong accepted Jian's memorial and therefore ordered beating with the rod and banishment to the far south.

sentences.zh: 睿宗即位，堅自刑部侍郎加銀青光祿大夫，拜左散騎常侍，俄轉黃門侍郎。

translations.literal: When Emperor Ruizong took the throne, Jian rose from vice minister of justice to silver-blue glory grand master, was appointed Left Regular Attendant, and soon transferred to Yellow Gate vice minister.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Ruizong took the throne, Jian rose from vice minister of justice to silver-blue glory grand master, was appointed Left Regular Attendant, and soon transferred to Yellow Gate vice minister.

sentences.zh: 時監察御史李知古請兵以擊姚州西貳河蠻，既降附，又請築城，重征稅之。

translations.literal: At that time investigating censor Li Zhigu requested troops to attack the Xi'er River barbarians west of Yao Prefecture; after they had submitted, he again requested to build a city and heavily levied taxes on them.
translations.idiomatic: At that time investigating censor Li Zhigu requested troops to attack the Xi'er River tribes west of Yao Prefecture. After they had submitted, he again requested to build a city and heavily levied taxes on them.

sentences.zh: 堅以蠻夷生梗，可以羈縻屬之，未得同華夏之制，勞師涉遠，所損不補所獲，獨建議以為不便。

translations.literal: Jian held that the barbarians were naturally obstinate and could be kept subordinate through loose reins; they could not yet be treated by the same system as the Central States. To weary the army on distant expeditions—the losses would not repay the gains—and he alone memorialized that it was inexpedient.
translations.idiomatic: Jian held that the tribes were naturally obstinate and could be kept subordinate through loose reins; they could not yet be governed by the same system as the Central States. To weary the army on distant expeditions would cost more than it gained, and he alone memorialized that the plan was inexpedient.

sentences.zh: 睿宗不從，令知古發劍南兵往築城，將以列置州縣。

translations.literal: Ruizong did not follow his advice and ordered Zhigu to dispatch Jiannan troops to build the city, intending to array prefectures and districts there.
translations.idiomatic: Ruizong did not follow his advice and ordered Zhigu to dispatch Jiannan troops to build the city, intending to establish prefectures and districts there.

sentences.zh: 知古因是欲誅其豪傑，沒子女以為奴婢。

translations.literal: Zhigu thereby wished to execute their leading men and seize sons and daughters to make them slaves.
translations.idiomatic: Zhigu thereby wished to execute their leaders and seize sons and daughters to make them slaves.

sentences.zh: 蠻眾恐懼，乃殺知古，相率反叛，役徒奔潰，姚、巂路由是歷年不通。

translations.literal: The barbarian masses were terrified and therefore killed Zhigu; they rose in rebellion together, laborers and soldiers fled in rout, and the routes through Yao and Xie were blocked for years.
translations.idiomatic: The tribes were terrified and killed Zhigu. They rose in rebellion together, laborers and soldiers fled in rout, and the routes through Yao and Xie were blocked for years.

sentences.zh: 堅妻即侍中岑羲之妹，堅以與羲近親，固辭機密，乃轉太子詹事，謂人曰：「非敢求高，蓋避難也。」

translations.literal: Jian's wife was the younger sister of Palace Attendant Cen Xi. Because Jian was a close kinsman of Xi, he firmly declined confidential posts and was transferred to crown prince household steward, saying to others: "It is not that I dare seek high rank—I am avoiding disaster."
translations.idiomatic: Jian's wife was the younger sister of Palace Attendant Cen Xi. Because Jian was a close kinsman of Xi, he firmly declined confidential posts and was transferred to crown prince household steward, saying, "It is not that I dare seek high rank—I am avoiding disaster."

sentences.zh: 及羲誅，堅竟免坐累。

translations.literal: When Xi was executed, Jian in the end escaped being implicated.
translations.idiomatic: When Xi was executed, Jian escaped being implicated.

sentences.zh: 出為絳州刺史，五轉復入為秘書監。

translations.literal: He went out as governor of Jiang Prefecture; after five transfers he returned as director of the Secretariat.
translations.idiomatic: He went out as governor of Jiang Prefecture. After five transfers he returned as director of the Secretariat.

sentences.zh: 開元十三年，再遷左散騎常侍。

translations.literal: In the thirteenth year of Kaiyuan he was again transferred to Left Regular Attendant.
translations.idiomatic: In the thirteenth year of Kaiyuan he was again promoted to Left Regular Attendant.

sentences.zh: 其年，玄宗改麗正書院為集賢院，以堅為學士，副張說知院事，累封東海郡公。

translations.literal: That year Emperor Xuanzong changed the Lizheng Academy to the Hall of Assembled Worthies, appointed Jian as academician and deputy to Zhang Yue in managing the hall, and repeatedly enfeoffed him as Duke of Donghai commandery.
translations.idiomatic: That year Emperor Xuanzong changed the Lizheng Academy to the Hall of Assembled Worthies, appointed Jian as academician and deputy to Zhang Yue in managing the hall, and repeatedly enfeoffed him as Duke of Donghai commandery.

sentences.zh: 以修東封儀註及從升太山之功，特加光祿大夫。

translations.literal: Because of his merit in revising the eastern feng ceremonial regulations and accompanying the ascent of Mount Tai, he was specially given the glory grand master title.
translations.idiomatic: Because of his merit in revising the eastern feng ceremonial regulations and accompanying the ascent of Mount Tai, he was specially granted the glory grand master title.

sentences.zh: 堅多識典故，前後修撰格式、氏族及國史等，凡七入書府，時論美之。

translations.literal: Jian knew many canonical precedents; before and after he compiled formats, clans and surnames, and the national history, entering the book repository seven times in all, and public opinion praised him.
translations.idiomatic: Jian knew many canonical precedents. He compiled formats, genealogies, and the national history, entering the book repository seven times in all, and was widely praised.

sentences.zh: 十七年卒，年七十餘。

translations.literal: In the seventeenth year he died at age seventy-some.
translations.idiomatic: In the seventeenth year he died at the age of seventy-some.

sentences.zh: 上深悼惜之，遣中使就家吊，內出絹布以賻，贈太子少保，謚曰文。

translations.literal: The emperor deeply mourned him, sent a palace envoy to offer condolences at his home, issued silk and cloth from the inner storehouse as funeral gifts, posthumously appointed him Junior Tutor to the Heir Apparent, and gave him the posthumous title Wen.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor deeply mourned him, sent a palace envoy to offer condolences at his home, issued silk and cloth from the inner storehouse as funeral gifts, posthumously appointed him Junior Tutor to the Heir Apparent, and gave him the posthumous title Wen.

sentences.zh: 堅長姑為太宗充容，次姑為高宗婕妤，並有文藻。

translations.literal: Jian's elder aunt was a filling concubine to Emperor Taizong; his next aunt was a talented lady to Emperor Gaozong—both had literary grace.
translations.idiomatic: Jian's elder aunt was a filling concubine to Emperor Taizong; his next aunt was a talented lady to Emperor Gaozong. Both had literary grace.

sentences.zh: 堅父子以詞學著聞，議者方之漢世班氏。

translations.literal: Jian and his father and son were famed for literary learning, and commentators compared them to the Ban clan of Han times.
translations.idiomatic: Jian and his father and son were famed for literary learning, and commentators compared them to the Ban clan of Han times.

sentences.zh: 元行沖，河南人，後魏常山王素連之後也。

translations.literal: Yuan Xingchong—Yuan Xingchong was a man of Henan, a descendant of Northern Wei Prince of Changshan Sulian.
translations.idiomatic: Yuan Xingchong was a man of Henan, a descendant of Northern Wei Prince of Changshan Sulian.

sentences.zh: 少孤，為外祖司農卿韋機所養。

translations.literal: Orphaned in youth, he was raised by his maternal grandfather, Minister of Agriculture Wei Ji.
translations.idiomatic: Orphaned in youth, he was raised by his maternal grandfather, Minister of Agriculture Wei Ji.

sentences.zh: 博學多通，尤善音律及詁訓之書。

translations.literal: Broadly learned and widely versed, he was especially skilled in music and pitch and in exegetical books.
translations.idiomatic: Broadly learned and widely versed, he was especially skilled in music theory and exegetical studies.

sentences.zh: 舉進士，累轉通事舍人，納言狄仁傑甚重之。

translations.literal: He passed the jinshi examination and was repeatedly transferred to Master of Communications; Censor-in-Chief Di Renjie greatly valued him.
translations.idiomatic: He passed the jinshi examination and was repeatedly transferred to Master of Communications. Censor-in-Chief Di Renjie greatly valued him.

sentences.zh: 行沖性不阿順，多進規誡，嘗謂仁傑曰：「下之事上，亦猶蓄聚以自資也。

translations.literal: Xingchong's nature was not compliant; he often offered admonitions and warnings and once said to Renjie: "The inferior serving the superior is also like storing up supplies to support oneself.
translations.idiomatic: Xingchong was not compliant by nature and often offered admonitions. He once said to Renjie, "The inferior serving the superior is like storing up supplies to support oneself.

sentences.zh: 譬貴家儲積，則脯臘膎胰以供滋膳，參術芝桂以防屙疾。

translations.literal: It is like a noble household's stores: cured meats, pickled meats, fat, and tripe to supply rich fare; ginseng, atractylodes, ganoderma, and cassia to guard against illness.
translations.idiomatic: It is like a noble household's stores: cured meats, pickled meats, fat, and tripe to supply rich fare; ginseng, atractylodes, ganoderma, and cassia to guard against illness.

sentences.zh: 伏想門下賓客，堪充旨味者多，願以小人備一藥物。」

translations.literal: I venture to think that among your lordship's guests many could serve as fine flavors; I wish to have this petty man serve as one medicine."
translations.idiomatic: I venture to think that among your guests many could serve as fine fare. I wish to have this petty man serve as one medicine."

sentences.zh: 仁傑笑而謂人曰：「此吾藥籠中物，何可一日無也！」

translations.literal: Renjie laughed and said to others: "This is an item in my medicine chest—how could I be without it for a single day!"
translations.idiomatic: Renjie laughed and said to others, "This is an item in my medicine chest—how could I be without it for a single day!"

sentences.zh: 九遷至陜州刺史，兼隴右、關內兩道按察使，未行，拜太常少卿。

translations.literal: After nine transfers he reached governor of Shan Prefecture and concurrently surveillance commissioner of Longyou and Guannei circuits; before departing he was appointed vice director of the Court of Imperial Sacrifices.
translations.idiomatic: After nine transfers he reached governor of Shan Prefecture and concurrently surveillance commissioner of Longyou and Guannei circuits. Before departing he was appointed vice director of the Court of Imperial Sacrifices.

sentences.zh: 行沖以本族出於後魏，而未有編年之史，乃撰《魏典》三十卷，事詳文簡，為學者所稱。

translations.literal: Because his clan came from Later Wei yet had no annalistic history, he composed Wei Canon in thirty scrolls, detailed in events and concise in wording, and was praised by scholars.
translations.idiomatic: Because his clan came from Later Wei yet had no annalistic history, he composed Wei Canon in thirty scrolls, detailed in events and concise in wording, and was praised by scholars.

sentences.zh: 初魏明帝時，河西柳谷瑞石有牛繼馬後之象，魏收舊史以為晉元帝是牛氏之子，冒姓司馬，以應石文。

translations.literal: Earlier, in Emperor Ming of Wei's time, an auspicious stone at Willow Valley in Hexi had the image of an ox succeeded by a horse. Wei Shou's old history held that Emperor Yuan of Jin was a son of the Niu clan who took the surname Sima falsely, to match the stone text.
translations.idiomatic: Earlier, in Emperor Ming of Wei's time, an auspicious stone at Willow Valley in Hexi had the image of an ox succeeded by a horse. Wei Shou's old history held that Emperor Yuan of Jin was a son of the Niu clan who falsely took the surname Sima to match the stone text.

sentences.zh: 行沖推尋事跡，以後魏昭成帝名犍，繼晉受命，考校謠讖，著論以明之。

translations.literal: Xingchong traced the events and held that Later Wei's Emperor Zhaocheng, named Jian, succeeded Jin in receiving the mandate; he collated songs and prophecies and wrote a treatise to clarify this.
translations.idiomatic: Xingchong traced the events and held that Later Wei's Emperor Zhaocheng, named Jian, succeeded Jin in receiving the mandate. He collated songs and prophecies and wrote a treatise to clarify this.

sentences.zh: 開元初，自太子詹事出為岐州刺史，又充關內道按察使。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Kaiyuan he went out from crown prince household steward to governor of Qi Prefecture and again served as surveillance commissioner of Guannei circuit.
translations.idiomatic: Early in the Kaiyuan era he went out from crown prince household steward to governor of Qi Prefecture and again served as surveillance commissioner of Guannei circuit.

sentences.zh: 行沖自以書生不堪博擊之任，固辭按察，乃以寧州刺史崔琬代焉。

translations.literal: Xingchong, considering himself a scholar unfit for the duty of broad investigation, firmly declined surveillance and had Ning Prefecture governor Cui Wan replace him.
translations.idiomatic: Xingchong, considering himself a scholar unfit for the duty of broad investigation, firmly declined surveillance and had Ning Prefecture governor Cui Wan replace him.

sentences.zh: 俄復入為右散騎常侍、東都副留守。

translations.literal: Soon he returned as Right Regular Attendant and eastern capital deputy regent.
translations.idiomatic: Soon he returned as Right Regular Attendant and eastern capital deputy regent.

sentences.zh: 時嗣彭王誌暕庶兄誌謙被人誣告謀反，考訊自誣，繫獄待報，連坐十數人，行沖察其冤濫，並奏原之。

translations.literal: At that time Zhiqian, the elder brother by a different mother of Heir Apparent Prince of Peng Zhisui, was falsely accused of plotting rebellion; under interrogation he confessed falsely, was imprisoned awaiting sentence, and more than ten were implicated. Xingchong saw that the case was unjust and excessive and memorialized to pardon them all.
translations.idiomatic: At that time Zhiqian, the elder half-brother of Heir Apparent Prince of Peng Zhisui, was falsely accused of plotting rebellion. Under interrogation he confessed falsely, was imprisoned awaiting sentence, and more than ten were implicated. Xingchong saw that the case was unjust and memorialized to pardon them all.

sentences.zh: 四遷大理卿。

translations.literal: He was transferred four times to director of the Court of Judicial Review.
translations.idiomatic: He was promoted four times to director of the Court of Judicial Review.

sentences.zh: 時揚州長史李傑為侍御史王旭所陷，詔下大理結罪，行沖以傑歷政清貞，不宜枉為讒邪所構，又奏請從輕條出之。

translations.literal: At that time Yang Prefecture chief administrator Li Jie was framed by attendant censor Wang Xu; an edict ordered the Court of Judicial Review to fix guilt. Xingchong held that Jie, through successive administrations, had been pure and upright and should not be wrongly framed by slanderous villains, and again memorialized to release him under a lighter statute.
translations.idiomatic: At that time Yang Prefecture chief administrator Li Jie was framed by attendant censor Wang Xu. An edict ordered the Court of Judicial Review to fix guilt. Xingchong held that Jie had been pure and upright through successive administrations and should not be wrongly framed, and again memorialized to release him under a lighter statute.

sentences.zh: 當時雖不見從，深為時論所美。

translations.literal: Although at the time his advice was not followed, he was deeply praised in public opinion.
translations.idiomatic: Although at the time his advice was not followed, he was deeply praised in public opinion.

sentences.zh: 俄又固辭刑獄之官，求為散職。

translations.literal: Soon he again firmly declined judicial posts and sought a loose office.
translations.idiomatic: Soon he again firmly declined judicial posts and sought a loose office.

sentences.zh: 七年，復轉左散騎常侍。

translations.literal: In the seventh year he was again transferred to Left Regular Attendant.
translations.idiomatic: In the seventh year he was again promoted to Left Regular Attendant.

sentences.zh: 九遷國子祭酒，月餘，拜太子賓客、弘文館學士。

translations.literal: After nine transfers he became National University chancellor; a month later he was appointed crown prince guest and academician of the Hongwen Hall.
translations.idiomatic: After nine transfers he became National University chancellor. A month later he was appointed crown prince guest and academician of the Hongwen Hall.

sentences.zh: 累封常山郡公。

translations.literal: He was repeatedly enfeoffed as Duke of Changshan commandery.
translations.idiomatic: He was repeatedly enfeoffed as Duke of Changshan commandery.
