translations.idiomatic: From this time onward, only Zheng Gong was exalted.

sentences.zh: 王粲稱伊、洛已東，淮、漢之北，一人而已，莫不宗焉。

translations.literal: Wang Can said that east of Yi and Luo, north of Huai and Han, there was only one man, and none did not take him as master.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Can said that east of Yi and Luo, north of Huai and Han, there was only one man, and none did not take him as master.

sentences.zh: 咸云先儒多闕，鄭氏道備，粲竊嗟怪，因求其學。

translations.literal: All said the former Confucians had many lacunae and the Zheng school was complete; Can privately marveled and therefore sought his learning.
translations.idiomatic: All said the former Confucians had many lacunae and the Zheng school was complete. Can privately marveled and therefore sought his learning.

sentences.zh: 得《尚書註》，退而思之，以盡其意，意皆盡矣。

translations.literal: Obtaining the Commentary on the Documents, he withdrew to ponder it to exhaust its meaning—and the meanings were all exhausted.
translations.idiomatic: Obtaining the Commentary on the Documents, he withdrew to ponder it to exhaust its meaning—and the meanings were all exhausted.

sentences.zh: 所疑之者，猶未喻焉。

translations.literal: What he doubted, he still did not understand.
translations.idiomatic: What he doubted, he still did not understand.

sentences.zh: 凡有兩卷，列於其集。

translations.literal: In all there were two scrolls, listed in his collected works.
translations.idiomatic: In all there were two scrolls, listed in his collected works.

sentences.zh: 又王肅改鄭六十八條，張融核之，將定臧否。

translations.literal: Again Wang Su changed Zheng in sixty-eight articles; Zhang Rong examined them, about to decide approval or rejection.
translations.idiomatic: Again Wang Su changed Zheng in sixty-eight articles. Zhang Rong examined them, about to decide approval or rejection.

sentences.zh: 融稱玄註泉深廣博，兩漢四百餘年，未有偉於玄者。

translations.literal: Rong said Xuan's commentary was deep as a spring and vast; in the more than four hundred years of the two Han dynasties, none was greater than Xuan.
translations.idiomatic: Rong said Xuan's commentary was deep as a spring and vast; in the more than four hundred years of the two Han dynasties, none was greater than Xuan.

sentences.zh: 然二郊之祭，殊天之祀，此玄誤也。

translations.literal: Yet the sacrifices of the two suburbs and the distinct rites to Heaven—here Xuan erred.
translations.idiomatic: Yet the sacrifices of the two suburbs and the distinct rites to Heaven—here Xuan erred.

sentences.zh: 其如皇天祖所自出之帝，亦玄慮之失也。

translations.literal: Likewise regarding the Emperor from whom the imperial ancestor sprang as the august Heaven—this too was a lapse in Xuan's consideration.
translations.idiomatic: Likewise regarding the Emperor from whom the imperial ancestor sprang as the august Heaven—this too was a lapse in Xuan's consideration.

sentences.zh: 及服虔釋《傳》，未免差違，後代言之，思弘聖意，非謂揚己之善，掩人之名也。

translations.literal: When Fu Qian explained the Tradition, he inevitably had discrepancies; speaking for later ages, I think to expand the sage's intent—not to say exalt one's own merit or conceal others' fame.
translations.idiomatic: When Fu Qian explained the Tradition, he inevitably had discrepancies. Speaking for later ages, I think to expand the sage's intent—not to exalt one's own merit or conceal others' fame.

sentences.zh: 何者？

translations.literal: Why?
translations.idiomatic: Why?

sentences.zh: 君子用心，願聞其過，故仲尼曰：『過也人皆見之，更也人皆仰之』是也。

translations.literal: The gentleman in his purpose wishes to hear his faults; therefore Confucius said: 'When one errs, all see it; when one reforms, all look up to him'—that is so.
translations.idiomatic: The gentleman in his purpose wishes to hear his faults. Therefore Confucius said: 'When one errs, all see it; when one reforms, all look up to him'—that is so.

sentences.zh: 而專門之徒，恕己及物，或攻先師之誤，如聞父母之名，將謂亡者之德言而見壓於重壤也。

translations.literal: Yet specialists in one school, forgiving themselves and extending it to others, when attacking the former master's errors are like hearing their parents' names—taking the deceased's virtuous words as being pressed down under heavy earth.
translations.idiomatic: Yet specialists in one school, forgiving themselves and extending it to others, when attacking the former master's errors are like hearing their parents' names—taking the deceased's virtuous words as being pressed down under heavy earth.

sentences.zh: 故王劭《史論》曰：『魏、晉浮華，古道夷替，洎王肅、杜預，更開門戶。

translations.literal: Therefore Wang Shao's "Historical Discourse" says: 'Wei and Jin were florid; the ancient way was leveled and replaced; down to Wang Su and Du Yu, each opened a new gate.
translations.idiomatic: Therefore Wang Shao's "Historical Discourse" says: 'Wei and Jin were florid; the ancient way was leveled and replaced. Down to Wang Su and Du Yu, each opened a new gate.

sentences.zh: 歷載三百，士大夫恥為章句。

translations.literal: For three hundred years scholars and officials were ashamed to practice chapter and clause.
translations.idiomatic: For three hundred years scholars and officials were ashamed to practice chapter and clause.

sentences.zh: 唯草野生以專經自許，不能究覽異義，擇從其善。

translations.literal: Only rough fellows of the wild claimed specialization in the classics, unable to examine different interpretations and choose what was good.
translations.idiomatic: Only rough fellows of the wild claimed specialization in the classics, unable to examine different interpretations and choose what was good.

sentences.zh: 徒欲父康成，兄子慎，寧道孔聖誤，諱聞鄭、服非。

translations.literal: They merely wanted to call Kang Cheng father and Zifu Shen brother—preferring to say Confucius erred rather than hear that Zheng and Fu were wrong.
translations.idiomatic: They merely wanted to call Kang Cheng father and Zifu Shen brother—preferring to say Confucius erred rather than hear that Zheng and Fu were wrong.

sentences.zh: 然於鄭、服甚憒憒，鄭、服之外皆仇也。』」

translations.literal: Yet toward Zheng and Fu they were very muddled; outside Zheng and Fu all were enemies.'"
translations.idiomatic: Yet toward Zheng and Fu they were very muddled; outside Zheng and Fu all were enemies.'"

sentences.zh: 則知變易章句，其難五也。

translations.literal: Thus we know that changing chapter and clause—difficulty number five.
translations.idiomatic: Thus we know that changing chapter and clause—this is the fifth difficulty.

sentences.zh: 「伏以安國《尚書》、劉歆《左傳》，悉遭擯於曩葉，見重於來今。

translations.literal: "I submit that Kong Anguo's Documents and Liu Xin's Zuo Tradition were both rejected in former ages and are esteemed in the present.
translations.idiomatic: "I submit that Kong Anguo's Documents and Liu Xin's Zuo Tradition were both rejected in former ages and are esteemed in the present.

sentences.zh: 故知二人之鑒，高於漢廷遠矣。

translations.literal: Thus we know these two men's discernment far surpassed the Han court.
translations.idiomatic: Thus we know these two men's discernment far surpassed the Han court.

sentences.zh: 孔秀產云：『物極則變。

translations.literal: Kong Xiuchan said: 'When things reach the extreme they change.
translations.idiomatic: Kong Xiuchan said: 'When things reach the extreme they change.

sentences.zh: 比及百年外，當有明直君子，恨不與吾同代者。』

translations.literal: Within a hundred years hence there will surely be a bright and upright gentleman who will regret not being of my generation.'
translations.idiomatic: Within a hundred years hence there will surely be a bright and upright gentleman who will regret not being of my generation.'

sentences.zh: 於戲！

translations.literal: Alas!
translations.idiomatic: Alas!

sentences.zh: 道之行廢，必有其時者歟！

translations.literal: Whether the Way is pursued or abandoned must have its time!
translations.idiomatic: Whether the Way is pursued or abandoned must have its time!

sentences.zh: 仆非專經，罕習章句，高名不著，易受經誣。

translations.literal: I am not a specialist in the classics, rarely practiced in chapter and clause; my high name is not established—I am easily subject to calumny for the classics.
translations.idiomatic: I am not a specialist in the classics, rarely practiced in chapter and clause. My high name is not established—I am easily subject to calumny for the classics.

sentences.zh: 頃者修撰，殆淹年月，賴諸賢輩能左右之，免致愆尤，仍叨賞賫，內省昏朽，其榮已多。

translations.literal: Recently in compilation I nearly spent a full year; relying on various worthies to assist me, I escaped fault and still received rewards; reflecting within on my dull decay, the honor is already more than enough.
translations.idiomatic: Recently in compilation I nearly spent a full year. Relying on various worthies to assist me, I escaped fault and still received rewards. Reflecting within on my dull decay, the honor is already more than enough.

sentences.zh: 何遽持一己之區區，抗群情之噂沓褷，舍勿矜之美，成自我之私，觸近名之誡，興犯眾之禍？

translations.literal: Why hasten to hold one's petty private view against the clamoring crowd, abandon the beauty of not boasting, accomplish self-serving private ends, touch the admonition against chasing fame, and invite the calamity of offending the multitude?
translations.idiomatic: Why hasten to hold one's petty private view against the clamoring crowd, abandon the beauty of not boasting, accomplish self-serving private ends, touch the admonition against chasing fame, and invite the calamity of offending the multitude?

sentences.zh: 一舉四失，中材不為，是用韜聲，甘此沈默也。」」

translations.literal: Four errors in one act—men of average ability will not do it; therefore I conceal my voice and willingly accept this silence.""
translations.idiomatic: Four errors in one act—men of average ability will not do it. Therefore I conceal my voice and willingly accept this silence.""

sentences.zh: 行沖俄又累表請致仕，制許之。

translations.literal: Before long Xingchong repeatedly memorialized requesting retirement, and an edict permitted it.
translations.idiomatic: Before long Xingchong repeatedly memorialized requesting retirement, and an edict permitted it.

sentences.zh: 十七年卒，年七十七，贈禮部尚書，謚曰獻。

translations.literal: In the seventeenth year he died at age seventy-seven; he was posthumously appointed minister of rites and given the posthumous title Xian.
translations.idiomatic: In the seventeenth year he died at the age of seventy-seven. He was posthumously appointed minister of rites and given the posthumous title Xian.

sentences.zh: 吳兢，汴州浚儀人也。

translations.literal: Wu Jing—Wu Jing was a native of Junyi in Bian Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: Wu Jing was a native of Junyi in Bian Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 勵誌勤學，博通經史。

translations.literal: He strengthened his will and studied diligently, broadly mastering the classics and histories.
translations.idiomatic: He strengthened his will and studied diligently, broadly mastering the classics and histories.

sentences.zh: 宋州人魏元忠、亳州人硃敬則深器重之，及居相輔，薦兢有史才，堪居近侍，因令直史館，修國史。

translations.literal: Wei Yuanzhong of Song Prefecture and Zhu Jingze of Bo Prefecture deeply valued him; when they served as chief ministers they recommended that Jing had historiographical talent fit for close attendance, and therefore ordered him to serve directly in the History Office and compile the national history.
translations.idiomatic: Wei Yuanzhong of Song Prefecture and Zhu Jingze of Bo Prefecture deeply valued him. When they served as chief ministers they recommended that Jing had historiographical talent fit for close attendance and ordered him to serve directly in the History Office and compile the national history.

sentences.zh: 累月，拜右拾遺內供奉。

translations.literal: After several months he was appointed Right Reminder with inner attendance.
translations.idiomatic: After several months he was appointed Right Reminder with inner attendance.

sentences.zh: 神龍中，遷右補闕，與韋承慶、崔融、劉子玄撰《則天實錄》成，轉起居郎。

translations.literal: During Shenlong he was transferred to Right Reminder and, with Wei Chengqing, Cui Rong, and Liu Zixuan, completed compilation of the Veritable Record of Empress Zetian, then was transferred to Attendant of the Bedchamber.
translations.idiomatic: During the Shenlong era he was transferred to Right Reminder and, with Wei Chengqing, Cui Rong, and Liu Zixuan, completed the Veritable Record of Empress Zetian, then was transferred to Attendant of the Bedchamber.

sentences.zh: 俄遷水部郎中，丁憂還鄉里。

translations.literal: Soon he was transferred to director of the Bureau of Waterways, entered mourning, and returned to his home district.
translations.idiomatic: Soon he was transferred to director of the Bureau of Waterways, entered mourning, and returned home.

sentences.zh: 開元三年服闋，抗疏言曰：「臣修史已成數十卷，自停職還家，匪忘紙劄，乞終餘功。」

translations.literal: In the third year of Kaiyuan, when mourning ended, he submitted a forthright memorial, saying: "Your servant has already compiled several tens of scrolls of history; since leaving office and returning home I have not forgotten paper and brush—I beg to finish the remaining work."
translations.idiomatic: In the third year of Kaiyuan, when mourning ended, he submitted a forthright memorial saying, "I have already compiled several tens of scrolls of history. Since leaving office and returning home I have not forgotten paper and brush. I beg to finish the remaining work."

sentences.zh: 乃拜諫議大夫，依前修史。

translations.literal: He was then appointed Remonstrance Grand Master and compiled history as before.
translations.idiomatic: He was then appointed Remonstrance Grand Master and continued compiling history as before.

sentences.zh: 俄兼修文館學士，歷衛少卿、右庶子。

translations.literal: Soon he was concurrently academician of the Xiūwen Hall and served successively as vice director of the Guard and right vice director of the crown prince's palace.
translations.idiomatic: Soon he was concurrently academician of the Xiūwen Hall and served successively as vice director of the Guard and right vice director of the crown prince's palace.

sentences.zh: 居職殆三十年，敘事簡要，人用稱之。

translations.literal: He held office for nearly thirty years; his narration was concise and essential, and people praised him.
translations.idiomatic: He held office for nearly thirty years. His narration was concise and essential, and people praised him.

sentences.zh: 末年傷於太簡。

translations.literal: In his later years he suffered from being too concise.
translations.idiomatic: In his later years he was criticized for being too concise.

sentences.zh: 《國史》未成，十七年，出為荊州司馬，制許以史稿自隨。

translations.literal: The National History was not completed. In the seventeenth year he went out as military aide of Jing Prefecture; an edict permitted him to take his historical drafts with him.
translations.idiomatic: The National History was not completed. In the seventeenth year he went out as military aide of Jing Prefecture. An edict permitted him to take his historical drafts with him.

sentences.zh: 中書令蕭嵩監修國史，奏取兢所撰《國史》，得六十五卷。

translations.literal: Chief Minister Xiao Song supervised compilation of the national history and memorialized to take Jing's compiled National History, obtaining sixty-five scrolls.
translations.idiomatic: Chief Minister Xiao Song supervised compilation of the national history and memorialized to take Jing's compiled National History, obtaining sixty-five scrolls.

sentences.zh: 累遷臺、洪、饒、蘄四州刺史，加銀青光祿大夫，遷相州長垣縣子。

translations.literal: He was repeatedly transferred as governor of Tai, Hong, Rao, and Qi prefectures, given the silver-blue glory grand master title, and promoted to Viscount of Changyuan county in Xiang Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: He was repeatedly transferred as governor of Tai, Hong, Rao, and Qi prefectures, granted the silver-blue glory grand master title, and promoted to Viscount of Changyuan county in Xiang Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 天寶初改官名，為鄴郡太守，入為恆王傅。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Tianbao, when official titles were changed, he became governor of Ye commandery and entered service as tutor to the Prince of Heng.
translations.idiomatic: Early in the Tianbao era, when official titles were changed, he became governor of Ye commandery and entered service as tutor to the Prince of Heng.

sentences.zh: 兢嘗以梁、陳、齊、周、隋五代史繁雜，乃別撰《梁》、《齊》、《周史》各十卷、《陳史》五卷、《隋史》二十卷，又傷疏略。

translations.literal: Jing once found the histories of the five dynasties Liang, Chen, Qi, Zhou, and Sui too cumbersome and therefore separately composed Liang History, Qi History, and Zhou History in ten scrolls each, Chen History in five scrolls, and Sui History in twenty scrolls, yet was also faulted for being too sparse and brief.
translations.idiomatic: Jing once found the histories of Liang, Chen, Qi, Zhou, and Sui too cumbersome and therefore separately composed Liang History, Qi History, and Zhou History in ten scrolls each, Chen History in five scrolls, and Sui History in twenty scrolls, yet was also faulted for being too sparse.

sentences.zh: 兢雖衰耗，猶希史職，而行步傴僂，李林甫以其年老不用。

translations.literal: Although Jing was worn out by age, he still hoped for a historiographical post, but his gait was stooped; Li Linfu, because he was old, did not employ him.
translations.idiomatic: Although Jing was worn out by age, he still hoped for a historiographical post, but his gait was stooped. Li Linfu, because he was old, did not employ him.

sentences.zh: 天寶八年，卒於家，時年八十餘。

translations.literal: In the eighth year of Tianbao he died at home at age eighty-some.
translations.idiomatic: In the eighth year of Tianbao he died at home at the age of eighty-some.

sentences.zh: 兢卒後，其子進兢所撰《唐史》八十餘卷，事多紕繆，不逮於壯年。

translations.literal: After Jing died his son presented Jing's compiled Tang History in more than eighty scrolls; the events were often erroneous and did not reach the quality of his vigorous years.
translations.idiomatic: After Jing died his son presented Jing's compiled Tang History in more than eighty scrolls. The events were often erroneous and did not reach the quality of his vigorous years.

sentences.zh: 兢家聚書頗多，嘗目錄其卷第，號《吳氏西齋書目》。

translations.literal: Jing's household gathered many books; he once catalogued their fascicles under the title Wu Clan Western Studio Bibliography.
translations.idiomatic: Jing's household gathered many books. He once catalogued their fascicles under the title Wu Clan Western Studio Bibliography.

sentences.zh: 韋述，司農卿弘機曾孫也。

translations.literal: Wei Shu—Wei Shu was the great-grandson of Minister of Agriculture Wei Hongji.
translations.idiomatic: Wei Shu was the great-grandson of Minister of Agriculture Wei Hongji.

sentences.zh: 父景駿，房州刺史。

translations.literal: His father Jingjun was governor of Fang Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: His father Jingjun was governor of Fang Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 述少聰敏，篤誌文學。

translations.literal: Shu in youth was clever and keen, devoted in will to literary studies.
translations.idiomatic: Shu in youth was clever and keen and devoted himself to literary studies.

sentences.zh: 家有書二千卷，述為兒童時，記覽皆遍。

translations.literal: The family had two thousand scrolls of books; when Shu was a child he had read and reviewed them all.
translations.idiomatic: The family had two thousand scrolls of books. When Shu was a child he had read them all.

sentences.zh: 人駭異之。

translations.literal: People were startled and marveled at him.
translations.idiomatic: People were astonished.

sentences.zh: 景龍中，景駿為肥鄉令，述從父至任。

translations.literal: During Jinglong, Jingjun was magistrate of Feixiang; Shu followed his father to the post.
translations.idiomatic: During the Jinglong era Jingjun was magistrate of Feixiang. Shu followed his father to the post.

sentences.zh: 洺州刺史元行沖，景駿之姑子，為時大儒，常載書數車自隨。

translations.literal: Ming Prefecture governor Yuan Xingchong, Jingjun's nephew by marriage, was a great Confucian of the age and often carried several cartloads of books with him.
translations.idiomatic: Ming Prefecture governor Yuan Xingchong, Jingjun's nephew by marriage, was a great Confucian of the age and often carried several cartloads of books with him.

sentences.zh: 述入其書齋，忘寢與食。

translations.literal: Shu entered his book studio and forgot sleep and food.
translations.idiomatic: Shu entered his book studio and forgot sleep and food.

sentences.zh: 行沖異之，引與之談，貫穿經史，事如指掌，探賾奧旨，如遇師資。

translations.literal: Xingchong marveled at him and drew him into conversation; he penetrated the classics and histories, matters were like the palm of his hand, and in probing profound meanings he was as if meeting a teacher.
translations.idiomatic: Xingchong marveled at him and drew him into conversation. He penetrated the classics and histories as if matters lay in the palm of his hand, and in probing profound meanings he was like one meeting a teacher.

sentences.zh: 又試以綴文，操牘便就。

translations.literal: He was also tested in literary composition and, taking up the document, completed it at once.
translations.idiomatic: He was also tested in literary composition and, taking up the document, completed it at once.

sentences.zh: 行沖大悅，引之同榻曰：「此吾外家之寶也。」

translations.literal: Xingchong was greatly pleased and drew him to share his couch, saying: "This is a treasure of my wife's family."
translations.idiomatic: Xingchong was greatly pleased and drew him to share his couch, saying, "This is a treasure of my wife's family."

sentences.zh: 舉進士，西入關，時述甚少，儀形眇小。

translations.literal: He passed the jinshi examination and entered the pass to the west; at that time Shu was very young and slight in stature.
translations.idiomatic: He passed the jinshi examination and entered the pass to the west. At that time Shu was very young and slight in stature.

sentences.zh: 考功員外郎宋之問曰：「韋學士童年有何事業？」

translations.literal: Vice director of the Bureau of Evaluations Song Zhiwen asked: "What work has Academician Wei accomplished in his childhood?"
translations.idiomatic: Vice director of the Bureau of Evaluations Song Zhiwen asked, "What work has Academician Wei accomplished in his childhood?"

sentences.zh: 述對曰：「性好著書。

translations.literal: Shu replied: "My nature loves composing books.
translations.idiomatic: Shu replied, "My nature loves composing books.

sentences.zh: 述有所撰《唐春秋》三十卷，恨未終篇。

translations.literal: Shu has composed Tang Spring and Autumn in thirty scrolls and regrets that it is not yet finished.
translations.idiomatic: Shu has composed Tang Spring and Autumn in thirty scrolls and regrets that it is not yet finished.

sentences.zh: 至如詞策，仰待明試。」

translations.literal: As for literary compositions and policy essays, I look up to await the enlightened examination."
translations.idiomatic: As for literary compositions and policy essays, I await the official examination."

sentences.zh: 之問曰：「本求異才，果得遷、固。」

translations.literal: Zhiwen said: "I originally sought unusual talent and have indeed obtained a Ban or a Sima."
translations.idiomatic: Zhiwen said, "I originally sought unusual talent and have indeed obtained a Ban or a Sima."

sentences.zh: 是歲登科。

translations.literal: That year he passed the examination.
translations.idiomatic: That year he passed the examination.

sentences.zh: 開元五年，為櫟陽尉。

translations.literal: In the fifth year of Kaiyuan he became magistrate of Liyang.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifth year of Kaiyuan he became magistrate of Liyang.

sentences.zh: 秘書監馬懷素受詔編次圖書，乃奏用左散騎常侍元行沖、左庶子齊澣、秘書少監王珣、衛尉少卿吳兢並述等二十六人，同於秘閣詳錄四部書。

translations.literal: Secretariat director Ma HuaiSu received an edict to arrange books in order and memorialized to employ Left Regular Attendant Yuan Xingchong, left vice director of the crown prince's palace Qi Huan, Secretariat vice director Wang Xun, Guard vice director Wu Jing, and Shu and twenty-six others together in the Secret Repository to record in detail the four sections of books.
translations.idiomatic: Secretariat director Ma Huai Su received an edict to arrange the library and memorialized to employ Left Regular Attendant Yuan Xingchong, left vice director of the crown prince's palace Qi Huan, Secretariat vice director Wang Xun, Guard vice director Wu Jing, Shu, and twenty-six others to record the four bibliographic sections in detail at the Secret Repository.

sentences.zh: 懷素尋卒，行沖代掌其事，五年而成，其總目二百卷。

translations.literal: HuaiSu soon died; Xingchong took over the affair in his place, and in five years it was completed, its general catalogue being two hundred scrolls.
translations.idiomatic: Huai Su soon died. Xingchong took over the project, and in five years it was completed, its general catalogue running to two hundred scrolls.

sentences.zh: 述好譜學，秘閣中見常侍柳沖先撰《姓族系錄》二百卷，述於分課之外手自抄錄，暮則懷歸。

translations.literal: Shu loved genealogical studies; in the Secret Repository he saw Regular Attendant Liu Chong's earlier Genealogical Records of Clans and Surnames in two hundred scrolls, and beyond his assigned duties personally copied them by hand, carrying them home each evening.
translations.idiomatic: Shu loved genealogical studies. In the Secret Repository he saw Regular Attendant Liu Chong's Genealogical Records of Clans and Surnames in two hundred scrolls and, beyond his assigned duties, personally copied them by hand, carrying them home each evening.

sentences.zh: 如是周歲，寫錄皆畢，百氏源流，轉益詳悉。

translations.literal: In this way for a full year he finished copying and recording, and the origins and currents of the hundred clans became ever more detailed.
translations.idiomatic: In this way for a full year he finished copying and recording, and the origins of the hundred clans became ever more detailed.

sentences.zh: 乃於《柳錄》之中，別撰成《開元譜》二十卷。

translations.literal: He then, within Liu's Records, separately composed Kaiyuan Genealogies in twenty scrolls.
translations.idiomatic: He then, building on Liu's Records, separately composed Kaiyuan Genealogies in twenty scrolls.

sentences.zh: 其篤誌忘倦，皆此類也。

translations.literal: His steadfast will and forgetting weariness were all of this kind.
translations.idiomatic: His steadfast devotion and tireless labor were all of this kind.

sentences.zh: 轉右補闕，中書令張說專集賢院事，引述為直學士，遷起居舍人。

translations.literal: He was transferred to Right Reminder; Chief Minister Zhang Yue took sole charge of the Hall of Assembled Worthies and brought in Shu as direct academician, then transferred him to Attendant of the Bedchamber.
translations.idiomatic: He was transferred to Right Reminder. Chief Minister Zhang Yue took sole charge of the Hall of Assembled Worthies and brought in Shu as direct academician, then transferred him to Attendant of the Bedchamber.

sentences.zh: 說重詞學之士，述與張九齡、許景先、袁暉、趙冬曦、孫逖、王幹常遊其門。

translations.literal: Yue valued men of literary learning; Shu, together with Zhang Jiuling, Xu Jingxian, Yuan Hui, Zhao Dongxi, Sun Ti, and Wang Gan, often visited his gate.
translations.idiomatic: Yue valued men of literary learning. Shu, together with Zhang Jiuling, Xu Jingxian, Yuan Hui, Zhao Dongxi, Sun Ti, and Wang Gan, often visited his household.

sentences.zh: 趙冬曦兄冬日，弟知壁、居貞、安貞、頤貞等六人，述弟迪、逌、迥、起、巡亦六人，並詞學登科。

translations.literal: Zhao Dongxi's elder brother Dongri and younger brothers Zhibi, Juzhen, Anzhen, Yizhen, and four others—six in all—and Shu's younger brothers Di, You, Jiong, Qi, and Xun, also six, all passed examinations in literary learning.
translations.idiomatic: Zhao Dongxi's elder brother Dongri and younger brothers Zhibi, Juzhen, Anzhen, Yizhen, and three others—six in all—and Shu's younger brothers Di, You, Jiong, Qi, and Xun, also six, all passed examinations in literary learning.

sentences.zh: 說曰：「趙、韋昆季，令之杞梓也。」

translations.literal: Yue said: "The Zhao and Wei brothers are the catalpa and paulownia of our age."
translations.idiomatic: Yue said, "The Zhao and Wei brothers are the finest timber of our age."

sentences.zh: 十八年，兼知史官事，轉屯田員外郎、職方吏部二郎中，學士、知史官事如故。

translations.literal: In the eighteenth year he was concurrently put in charge of historiographical affairs, transferred to vice director of the Bureau of State Farms and director of the second rank in the Bureaus of Appointments and Personnel, and remained academician and in charge of historiographical affairs as before.
translations.idiomatic: In the eighteenth year he was concurrently put in charge of historiographical affairs, transferred to vice director of the Bureau of State Farms and director of the second rank in the Bureaus of Appointments and Personnel, and remained academician and in charge of historiographical affairs as before.

sentences.zh: 及張九齡為中書令，即集賢之同職，裴耀卿為侍中，即述之舅，皆相推重，語必移晷。

translations.literal: When Zhang Jiuling became chief minister—he had been Shu's colleague at the Hall of Assembled Worthies—and Pei Yaoqing became palace attendant—he was Shu's uncle by marriage—all mutually esteemed one another, and their conversations always lasted until the sundial had moved.
translations.idiomatic: When Zhang Jiuling became chief minister—he had been Shu's colleague at the Hall of Assembled Worthies—and Pei Yaoqing became palace attendant—he was Shu's uncle by marriage—all mutually esteemed one another, and their conversations always lasted for hours.

sentences.zh: 二十七年，轉國子司業，停知史事。

translations.literal: In the twenty-seventh year he was transferred to National University vice director and ceased overseeing historiographical affairs.
translations.idiomatic: In the twenty-seventh year he was transferred to National University vice director and ceased overseeing historiographical affairs.

sentences.zh: 俄而復兼史職，充集賢學士。

translations.literal: Soon he again concurrently held historiographical duties and served as academician of the Hall of Assembled Worthies.
translations.idiomatic: Soon he again concurrently held historiographical duties and served as academician of the Hall of Assembled Worthies.

sentences.zh: 天寶初，歷左右庶子，加銀青光祿大夫。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Tianbao he served successively as left and right vice director of the crown prince's palace and was given the silver-blue glory grand master title.
translations.idiomatic: Early in the Tianbao era he served successively as left and right vice director of the crown prince's palace and was granted the silver-blue glory grand master title.

sentences.zh: 九載，兼充禮儀使。

translations.literal: In the ninth year he was concurrently made commissioner of ritual.
translations.idiomatic: In the ninth year he was concurrently made commissioner of ritual.

sentences.zh: 其載遷尚書工部侍郎，封方城縣侯。

translations.literal: That year he was transferred to vice minister of works in the Secretariat and enfeoffed as Marquis of Fangcheng county.
translations.idiomatic: That year he was transferred to vice minister of works in the Secretariat and enfeoffed as Marquis of Fangcheng county.

sentences.zh: 述在書府四十年，居史職二十年，嗜學著書，手不釋卷。

translations.literal: Shu was in the book repository for forty years and held historiographical office for twenty years; he loved learning and composing books and never put down his scrolls.
translations.idiomatic: Shu was in the book repository for forty years and held historiographical office for twenty years. He loved learning and composing books and never put down his scrolls.

sentences.zh: 國史自令狐德棻至於吳兢，雖累修撰，竟未成一家之言。

translations.literal: The national history, from Linghu Defen to Wu Jing, although repeatedly revised and compiled, in the end did not achieve the words of a single school.
translations.idiomatic: The national history, from Linghu Defen to Wu Jing, although repeatedly revised and compiled, in the end did not achieve a unified work.

sentences.zh: 至述始定類例，補遺續闕，勒成《國史》一百一十二卷，並《史例》一卷，事簡而記詳，雅有良史之才，蘭陵蕭穎士以為譙周、陳壽之流。

translations.literal: Only with Shu were categories and examples first fixed, omissions supplemented and gaps continued, and the National History completed in one hundred twelve scrolls, together with Precedents in Historiography in one scroll—events concise yet records detailed, elegantly possessing the talent of a good historian. Lanling's Xiao Yingshi regarded him as in the stream of Qiao Zhou and Chen Shou.
translations.idiomatic: Only with Shu were categories and examples first fixed, omissions supplemented and gaps filled, and the National History completed in one hundred twelve scrolls, together with Precedents in Historiography in one scroll—events concise yet records detailed, elegantly possessing the talent of a good historian. Lanling's Xiao Yingshi regarded him as in the company of Qiao Zhou and Chen Shou.

sentences.zh: 述早以儒術進，當代宗仰，而純厚長者，淡於勢利，道之同者，無間貴賤，皆禮接之。

translations.literal: Shu early advanced through Confucian learning and was revered in his age; he was pure, generous, and a man of long standing, indifferent to power and profit. Those who shared his way, without regard to noble or base, he all received with courtesy.
translations.idiomatic: Shu early advanced through Confucian learning and was revered in his age. Pure, generous, and steady, he was indifferent to power and profit. Those who shared his way, without regard to rank, he all received with courtesy.

sentences.zh: 家聚書二萬卷，皆自校定鉛槧，雖禦府不逮也。

translations.literal: His household gathered twenty thousand scrolls of books, all personally collated with lead and wooden slips—even the imperial repository did not reach this.
translations.idiomatic: His household gathered twenty thousand scrolls of books, all personally collated—even the imperial repository did not match this.

sentences.zh: 兼古今朝臣圖，歷代知名人畫，魏、晉已來草隸真跡數百卷，古碑、古器、藥方、格式、錢譜、璽譜之類，當代名公尺題，無不畢備。

translations.literal: He also had portraits of court ministers ancient and modern, paintings of famous men through the ages, several hundred scrolls of cursive, clerical, and regular script autographs from Wei and Jin onward, ancient stelae, ancient vessels, medical formulas, formats, coin catalogues, seal catalogues, and the like, and short inscriptions by famous men of the age—all were fully provided.
translations.idiomatic: He also had portraits of court ministers ancient and modern, paintings of famous men through the ages, several hundred scrolls of calligraphic autographs from Wei and Jin onward, ancient stelae, ancient vessels, medical formulas, formats, coin catalogues, seal catalogues, and short inscriptions by famous men of the age—all were fully provided.

sentences.zh: 及祿山之亂，兩京陷賊，玄宗幸蜀，述抱《國史》藏於南山，經籍資產，焚剽殆盡。

translations.literal: When the rebellion of Lushan broke out, the two capitals fell to the rebels, and Emperor Xuanzong went to Shu, Shu carried the National History and hid it in the southern mountains; classics, records, and assets were burned and plundered almost entirely.
translations.idiomatic: When the rebellion of Lushan broke out, the two capitals fell to the rebels, and Emperor Xuanzong went to Shu. Shu carried the National History and hid it in the southern mountains. His classics, records, and assets were burned and plundered almost entirely.

sentences.zh: 述亦陷於賊庭，授偽官。

translations.literal: Shu also fell into the rebel court and was given a false office.
translations.idiomatic: Shu also fell into the rebel court and was given a false office.

sentences.zh: 至德二年，收兩京，三司議罪，流於渝州，為刺史薛舒困辱，不食而卒。

translations.literal: In the second year of Zhide the two capitals were recovered; the Three Offices deliberated guilt and banished him to Yu Prefecture, where he was humiliated by governor Xue Shu, stopped eating, and died.
translations.idiomatic: In the second year of Zhide the two capitals were recovered. The Three Offices deliberated guilt and banished him to Yu Prefecture, where he was humiliated by governor Xue Shu, stopped eating, and died.

sentences.zh: 其甥蕭直為太尉李光弼判官，廣德二年，直因入奏言事稱旨，乃上疏理述於蒼黃之際，能存《國史》，致聖朝大典，得無遺逸，以功補過，合霑恩宥。

translations.literal: His nephew Xiao Zhi was case judge to Grand Marshal Li Guangbi. In the second year of Guangde, because Zhi, on entering to memorialize on affairs, pleased the emperor, he submitted a memorial arguing that Shu, in the moment of crisis, had been able to preserve the National History and thereby ensured that the sacred court's great canon was not lost—merit should offset fault, and he ought to receive imperial grace and pardon.
translations.idiomatic: His nephew Xiao Zhi was case judge to Grand Marshal Li Guangbi. In the second year of Guangde, because Zhi, on entering to memorialize on affairs, pleased the emperor, he submitted a memorial arguing that Shu, in the moment of crisis, had preserved the National History and thereby ensured that the court's great canon was not lost—merit should offset fault, and he ought to receive imperial pardon.

sentences.zh: 乃贈右散騎常侍。

translations.literal: He was therefore posthumously appointed Right Regular Attendant.
translations.idiomatic: He was therefore posthumously appointed Right Regular Attendant.

sentences.zh: 議者云自唐已來，氏族之盛，無逾於韋氏。

translations.literal: Commentators said that since Tang times the flourishing of clans had not surpassed the Wei clan.
translations.idiomatic: Commentators said that since Tang times no clan had flourished more than the Wei clan.

sentences.zh: 其孝友詞學，承慶、嗣立為最；

translations.literal: In filial piety, friendship, and literary learning, Chengqing and Silizhi were foremost;
translations.idiomatic: In filial piety, friendship, and literary learning, Chengqing and Silizhi were foremost;

sentences.zh: 明於音律，則萬石為最；

translations.literal: in understanding music and pitch, Wanshi was foremost;
translations.idiomatic: in understanding music and pitch, Wanshi was foremost;

sentences.zh: 達於禮義，則叔夏為最；

translations.literal: in mastery of ritual and righteousness, Shuxia was foremost;
translations.idiomatic: in mastery of ritual and righteousness, Shuxia was foremost;

sentences.zh: 史才博識，以述為最。

translations.literal: in historiographical talent and broad knowledge, Shu was foremost.
translations.idiomatic: in historiographical talent and broad knowledge, Shu was foremost.

sentences.zh: 所撰《唐職儀》三十卷、《高宗實錄》三十卷、《御史臺記》十卷、《兩京新記》五卷，凡著書二百餘卷；

translations.literal: What he composed included Tang Official Rituals in thirty scrolls, Veritable Record of Emperor Gaozong in thirty scrolls, Record of the Censorate in ten scrolls, and New Record of the Two Capitals in five scrolls—in all more than two hundred scrolls of books;
translations.idiomatic: What he composed included Tang Official Rituals in thirty scrolls, Veritable Record of Emperor Gaozong in thirty scrolls, Record of the Censorate in ten scrolls, and New Record of the Two Capitals in five scrolls—in all more than two hundred scrolls;

sentences.zh: 皆行於代。

translations.literal: all circulated in his age.
translations.idiomatic: all circulated in his age.

sentences.zh: 述弟 逌逌，學業亦亞於述，尤精《三禮》，與述對為學士。

translations.literal: Shu's younger brother You—You's learning was also second only to Shu's; he was especially expert in the Three Rites and served as academician paired with Shu.
translations.idiomatic: Shu's younger brother You was second only to Shu in learning, especially expert in the Three Rites, and served as academician paired with Shu.

sentences.zh: 述弟 迪迪，同為禮官，時人榮之。

translations.literal: Shu's younger brother Di—Di likewise served as a ritual official, and people of the time regarded it as an honor.
translations.idiomatic: Shu's younger brother Di likewise served as a ritual official, and people of the time regarded it as an honor.

sentences.zh: 累遷考功員外郎、國子司業，以風疾卒。

translations.literal: He was repeatedly transferred to vice director of the Bureau of Evaluations and National University vice director and died of wind illness.
translations.idiomatic: He was repeatedly transferred to vice director of the Bureau of Evaluations and National University vice director and died of wind illness.

sentences.zh: 蕭穎士蕭穎士者，聰儁過人，富詞學，有名於時，賈曾、席豫、張垍及述皆引為談客。

translations.literal: Xiao Yingshi—Xiao Yingshi was surpassingly clever and rich in literary learning, famed in his time; Jia Zeng, Xi Yu, Zhang Ya, and Shu all brought him in as a conversational guest.
translations.idiomatic: Xiao Yingshi was surpassingly clever and rich in literary learning, famed in his time. Jia Zeng, Xi Yu, Zhang Ya, and Shu all brought him in as a conversational guest.

sentences.zh: 開元二十三年登進士第，考功員外郎孫逖稱之於朝。

translations.literal: In the twenty-third year of Kaiyuan he passed the jinshi examination; vice director of the Bureau of Evaluations Sun Ti praised him at court.
translations.idiomatic: In the twenty-third year of Kaiyuan he passed the jinshi examination. Vice director of the Bureau of Evaluations Sun Ti praised him at court.

sentences.zh: 褊躁無威儀，與時不偶，前後五授官，旋即駁落。

translations.literal: Narrow and irritable, without dignified bearing, he did not suit the age; five times he was given office and each time was soon dismissed.
translations.idiomatic: Narrow and irritable, without dignified bearing, he did not suit the age. Five times he was given office and each time was soon dismissed.

sentences.zh: 乾元初，終於揚府功曹。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Qianyuan he ended as merit officer of Yang Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: Early in the Qianyuan era he ended his career as merit officer of Yang Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 述在秘閣時，與鄠縣尉母煚、曹州司法殷踐猷並友善，二人相次卒。

translations.literal: When Shu was in the Secret Repository he was friendly with Huo county magistrate Wu Jiong and Cao Prefecture judicial aide Yin Jianyou; the two died in succession.
translations.idiomatic: When Shu was in the Secret Repository he was friendly with Huo county magistrate Wu Jiong and Cao Prefecture judicial aide Yin Jianyou. The two died in succession.

sentences.zh: 踐猷，申州刺史仲容從子，明《班史》，通於族姓。

translations.literal: Jianyou was the son of Shen Prefecture governor Zhongrong's younger brother; he understood the Ban histories and was versed in clans and surnames.
translations.idiomatic: Jianyou was the nephew of Shen Prefecture governor Zhongrong. He understood the Ban histories and was versed in clans and surnames.

sentences.zh: 子寅，有至性，早孤，事母以孝聞。

translations.literal: His son Yin had utmost nature; orphaned early, he was famed for filial service to his mother.
translations.idiomatic: His son Yin had utmost nature. Orphaned early, he was famed for filial service to his mother.

sentences.zh: 應宏詞舉，為永寧尉。

translations.literal: He responded to the broad phrases examination and became magistrate of Yongning.
translations.idiomatic: He responded to the broad phrases examination and became magistrate of Yongning.

sentences.zh: 史臣曰：前代文學之士，氣壹矣，然以道義偶乖，遭遇斯難。

translations.literal: The historiographer says: The literary scholars of former ages had unified spirit, yet because the way and righteousness occasionally went awry, they encountered such hardship.
translations.idiomatic: The historiographer says: The literary scholars of former ages had unified spirit, yet because the way and righteousness occasionally went awry, they encountered such hardship.

sentences.zh: 馬懷素、褚無量好古嗜學，博識多聞，遇好文之君，隆師資之禮，儒者之榮，可謂際會矣。

translations.literal: Ma HuaiSu and Chu Wuliang loved antiquity and were devoted to learning, broadly knowledgeable and widely heard; meeting a ruler who loved literature, they were honored with the rites due teachers—the glory of Confucians may be called a timely meeting.
translations.idiomatic: Ma Huai Su and Chu Wuliang loved antiquity and were devoted to learning, broadly knowledgeable and widely heard. Meeting a ruler who loved literature, they were honored with the rites due teachers—the glory of Confucians may be called a timely meeting.

sentences.zh: 劉、徐等五公，學際天人，才兼文史，俾西垣、東觀，一代粲然，蓋諸公之用心也。

translations.literal: The five lords Liu, Xu, and the others reached learning to Heaven and man and combined talent in literature and history, making the western wall and Eastern Pavilion brilliant for a generation—this was surely the intent of those gentlemen.
translations.idiomatic: The five lords Liu, Xu, and the others reached learning to Heaven and man and combined talent in literature and history, making the western wall and Eastern Pavilion brilliant for a generation—this was surely the intent of those gentlemen.

sentences.zh: 然而子玄郁結於當年，行沖仿徨於極筆，官不過俗吏，寵不逮常才，非過使然，蓋此道非趨時之具也，其窮也宜哉！

translations.literal: Yet Zixuan was pent up in his own day and Xingchong wandered at the final brush; their offices did not surpass common clerks and their favor did not reach ordinary talent—not because of fault, but because this path is not an instrument for suiting the times; their poverty was fitting!
translations.idiomatic: Yet Zixuan was pent up in his own day and Xingchong wandered at the final brush. Their offices did not surpass common clerks and their favor did not reach ordinary talent—not because of fault, but because this path is not an instrument for suiting the times. Their poverty was fitting!

sentences.zh: 贊贊曰：學者如市，博通甚難；

translations.literal: The eulogist says: Scholars are like a market; broad mastery is very hard;
translations.idiomatic: The eulogist says: Scholars are like a market; broad mastery is very hard;

sentences.zh: 文士措翰，典麗惟艱。

translations.literal: literary men set brush to paper—canonical elegance alone is difficult.
translations.idiomatic: literary men set brush to paper—canonical elegance alone is difficult.

sentences.zh: 馬、褚、兢、術，徐、元、子玄，文學之書，胡寧比焉！

translations.literal: Ma, Chu, Jing, and Shu, Xu, Yuan, and Zixuan—in books of literature, how could one compare!
translations.idiomatic: Ma, Chu, Jing, and Shu, Xu, Yuan, and Zixuan—in books of literature, who could compare!
